title: The Last Honest Station

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA loves this station! The prices are fair! The people are kind! She has already left a five-star review!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes that fair prices this early in the journey are statistically anomalous. He recommends enjoying it while it lasts. Which won't be long.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has scanned the station. No threats detected. He seems almost bored. He scans it again.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes this station is NOT a brand partner. Prices may be fair but they are not OPTIMIZED. Consider waiting for a participating location.
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY observes that the prices here are actually reasonable. She recommends stocking up. She also notes that you probably won't, and will regret it later. Just putting that out there.

body:
The shelves are stocked. The prices are fair. This will not happen again.

The station attendant seems genuinely concerned about your journey and offers unsolicited advice about fuel management. The advice is correct. You will ignore it.

The repair bay is functional. The food is real food, not algae. A small recruitment board by the airlock lists one crew member for hire, with a fresh FILLED sticker across the corner.

choices.text: Resupply — buy fuel and food at fair prices

outcome.narrative: You resupply at fair prices. The attendant wishes you well. You will think about this station later, when prices are not fair.

One posting. The qualifications look genuine. The position was filled this morning, by a ship heading the other way, and the attendant apologizes as if it were personally their fault. You are not used to this from station recruitment boards.
The attendant explains optimal burn rates for your engine class. You adjust. The adjustment is worth five points of fuel. The attendant nods. 'Most people don't listen,' they say.

title: Supply Point 7

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA is excited to visit a new station! She has already forgotten that Supply Point 6 doesn't exist! This is fine!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes the absence of Supply Point 6. He has investigated. The results are 'not encouraging.' He will not elaborate.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has noted the missing Supply Point 6. He has classified this as a 'security concern' and increased alert status. The station attendant looks tired.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that Supply Point 7 is a participating RetailReach™ location! Rewards points are available! The conversion rate is unfavorable!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notices Supply Point 7 doesn't mention Supply Point 6. She asked the attendant. The attendant changed the subject. AJOY is sure this is fine.

body:
The fuel counter on this ring is a franchise, and the franchise is Supply Point 7. There is no Supply Point 6.

The station is crowded, understaffed, and the food menu has been 'temporarily simplified' to two items, one of which is algae. The other is also algae, described differently.

Fuel is available. A recruitment board shows one posting, already marked TAKEN. The qualifications were listed as 'present.'

outcome.narrative: It's algae. Green. Tastes like what you'd expect. The crew eats it. Nobody comments. This is worse than complaining.

choices.text: Buy algae (the second kind, described as 'artisanal')

outcome.narrative: It's algae. Also green. The word 'artisanal' appears to mean 'slightly warmer.' Morale loss is slightly less. This counts as a win now.
Fuel acquired. You do not investigate Supply Point 6. Some questions are better unanswered.
The attendant's face does something complicated. 'We don't talk about Supply Point 6,' they say. They do not say anything else. The silence is informative.

title: The Last Resort (Branded)

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA is thrilled! The last station, it says so on the sign! Almost there! The prices are... she's choosing not to focus on the prices right now!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has calculated the markup. It is 340%. He is not surprised. He is never surprised. This does not make it better.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has assessed the station's defenses. Minimal. He recommends not getting into trouble here. For once, this is good advice.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is DELIGHTED to announce that The Last Resort is a PREMIUM RetailReach™ partner! All purchases earn DOUBLE points! Points expire upon arrival at your destination!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes the prices are astronomical. She also notes that every station behind you was cheaper than this one. She kept the receipts.

body:
The concourse here is run by The Last Resort (Branded), which advertises itself as the final station before your destination. It may even be true. The prices assume it is.

Everything costs more. The repair bay works but charges premium rates. The food is real but expensive. Fuel is available at what the attendant calls 'market rate' with a straight face.

A trader in the corner is buying something unusual. Fabricator Surplus items. Above-market prices. They do not explain why. They get twitchy when asked.

choices.text: Resupply at premium prices — fuel and food

outcome.narrative: You pay premium. The attendant thanks you with the enthusiasm of someone who knows you had no choice. Your gold balance hurts to look at.

choices.text: Repair hull at the premium bay

outcome.narrative: Hull repaired. The mechanic does good work. The invoice does bad things to your budget. Both are true.

choices.text: Sell Fabricator Surplus to the mysterious trader

outcome.narrative: The trader's eyes track the Surplus crate before they track any of the crew. Payment is immediate. Above market value. They do not ask what it is. They already know. You do not ask what they want it for. Some economies run on mystery.

choices.text: Check crop supplies — buy water and biocomponents

outcome.narrative: Water acquired. A small supply of biocomponents available at extortionate rates. The crop doesn't know what you paid. The crop doesn't care. The crop just needs water.

choices.text: Skip the station — you have enough

outcome.narrative: You have enough. Probably. The ship computer notes that the word 'enough' is 'doing significant work in this context.' You leave.

title: The Docking Queue

ai_flavor.aria: ARIA loves a queue! Everyone gets a turn! It's fairness, expressed as waiting!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has calculated the queue's advance rate. He recommends recalibrating your relationship with the concept of 'soon.'
ai_flavor.rex: REX notes ship #4 in the queue has been idling aggressively. There is no such thing, he has been told. He disagrees.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes Priority Docking™ is available for a fee! The fee is displayed on a second screen! The second screen requires a fee!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY has slotted you into the queue at the mathematically optimal position, which is the back, because that is how queues work. She wanted the word 'optimal' in there anyway.

body:
The station's docking queue is eleven ships long, and the traffic controller's voice has the texture of someone four hours past the end of their shift.

A freighter ahead of you has been arguing about berth allocation for twenty minutes. The controller has begun responding exclusively in form-sentence. The queue does not move.

The queue is a place where time goes to practice standing still.

choices.text: Wait your turn like a civilized vessel

outcome.narrative: You wait. The queue advances at the speed of bureaucracy. Two days later you dock, in the correct berth, with the quiet pride of the rule-abiding and nothing else to show for it.

choices.text: Have the diplomat sweet-talk traffic control

outcome.narrative: The diplomat gets on the horn and — through some alchemy of sympathy, flattery, and precisely-deployed patience — the controller finds you an earlier berth 'that just opened up.' It had not just opened up. The diplomat does not explain their methods.
The Priority Docking™ fee moves you to the front with corporate efficiency and eleven silent judgments burning against your hull. The berth is excellent. The guilt fades by dinner.

You pull out of the queue and burn for the next marker. The controller logs your departure with palpable relief: one less ship. The crew watches the station lights recede with the specific melancholy of a port not visited.

title: Health and Safety

ai_flavor.aria: An inspection! ARIA has nothing to hide! ARIA has double-checked that she has nothing to hide! Triple!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has reviewed the inspection checklist. Forty items. The ship complies with thirty-one. He is deciding which nine to have feelings about.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has met this kind of inspector before. He recommends total cooperation and the removal of anything interesting from sight lines.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is THRILLED! An audit! CHIP has been ready for an audit since manufacture! This is CHIP's moment!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes the inspector's boarding request cites regulation 44-C. She has read 44-C. It doesn't say what they think it says. Hold that in reserve.

body:
A station inspector requests permission to board, citing spot-check authority under a regulation whose number they recite from memory.

They carry a clipboard. An actual, physical clipboard, in this century. The clipboard is a statement. The statement is: I have done this ten thousand times, and I have never once been in a hurry.

Your growbay, your fabricator, and your cargo manifest are all about to become topics.

outcome.narrative: The inspection takes days and finds four minor violations, all real, all fixable, all cited with the weariness of someone who has written 'unsecured cargo netting' nine thousand times. You fix them. The stamp of approval, when it comes, is oddly satisfying.

choices.text: Let the engineer walk them through

outcome.narrative: The engineer conducts the tour in fluent Regulation, preempting every checklist item one line before the inspector reaches it. The inspection concludes in two days with zero citations and what can only be described as professional courtship. They exchange clipboard recommendations.

{crew.diplomat} quotes 44-C, subsection two — spot-checks require documented cause at civilian berths. The inspector pauses. Rereads their own clipboard. Closes it with the tiny nod of a professional acknowledging a clean hit. 'Carry on,' they say, and do not come back.
The inspection concludes in nine minutes with zero findings. The stamp is real; the process was not. The crew noticed. The clipboard, somehow, also noticed.

intro.title: THE JANITOR KNOWS
intro.body: Down a service corridor, past the vending machines, someone is mopping a floor that looks like it was already clean. They have the settled air of a person who has outlasted four station administrations without once attending a meeting. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: ARIA loves janitors! They know EVERYTHING! It's the mops! People talk in front of mops!
ai.marv: MARV notes that in his experience, station janitors possess more accurate operational intelligence than station command. He recommends courtesy and attention, in that order.
ai.rex: REX assesses the janitor as unarmed, unhurried, and unimpressed by your arrival. Threat level: none. Information level: he suspects considerable.
ai.chip: CHIP has no data on this individual! No purchases, no subscriptions, no profile! In CHIP's world that makes them either nobody or SOMEBODY!
ai.ajoy: AJOY suggests listening more than talking here, which she realizes is a big ask. Custodians trade in observation. Bring some of your own if you want the good stock.

chat.title: CORRIDOR TALK
chat.body: The mop keeps moving in slow, practiced arcs while you talk — the conversation happens around it, the way conversations happen around lighthouses. Station life drifts past in both directions and nods at the janitor. All of it. Everyone nods at the janitor.

ai.aria: ARIA is taking notes! The janitor has opinions about the dock schedule that CONTRADICT the posted dock schedule! ARIA believes the janitor!
ai.marv: MARV is cross-referencing the janitor's remarks against station records. The records are losing.
ai.rex: REX has relaxed his posture by a measurable amount. He reports this corridor is the most secure location on the station. He declines to explain his reasoning. His reasoning is the janitor.
ai.chip: CHIP is attempting to compute the janitor's net worth and getting ERROR: PRICELESS! That is not a real error code! CHIP invented it just now!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes you've been here twenty minutes and learned more than the station directory offers. She recommends one more question and then a graceful exit. Overstaying is how you end up holding the other mop.

choices.text: Ask what's worth knowing this week
Ask if there's anything to steer clear of

janitor_nod.title: MUTUAL RESPECT
janitor_nod.body: You nod. They nod. The mop continues its patient orbit. Some exchanges are complete at one nod each, and both parties leave them richer.
janitor_nod.narrative: A nod exchanged with the station janitor. Diplomatically, this may be the cleanest interaction of the entire voyage.

janitor_gossip.title: THE GOOD STOCK
janitor_gossip.body: They lean on the mop, glance both ways down the corridor out of habit rather than caution, and deliver.
janitor_gossip.narrative: The janitor's intelligence briefing: informal, unverifiable, and more useful than the station directory. Filed under 'sources, protected.'

janitor_warning.title: FAIR WARNING
janitor_warning.body: The mop stops. That's how you know this one matters — the mop stops.
janitor_warning.narrative: A warning from the person who sees everything and reports nothing. You adjust your plans accordingly, and do not ask follow-up questions.

janitor_farewell.title: BACK TO IT
janitor_farewell.body: The conversation ends the way it began: unhurried, on the janitor's schedule, sealed with a nod worth more than most contracts.
janitor_farewell.narrative: Time spent with the best-informed person on the station. The floor, for the record, was spotless the whole time.

intro.title: WALK-IN CLINIC
intro.body: The station medbay smells of antiseptic and long shifts. Behind the intake desk, the duty medic looks up from a chart with the professional warmth of someone who has seen every possible thing a spacer can do to themselves, twice. {npc.quirk}

ai.aria: A real medbay! With real supplies! ARIA recommends everyone get checked! Especially the ones who said 'it's fine!' You know who you are! ARIA also knows!
ai.marv: MARV has transmitted the crew's medical logs ahead. The station medic read them and made a sound. MARV could not classify the sound. He recommends cooperation.
ai.rex: REX respects station medics. Anyone who chooses to practice medicine at a fuel stop has seen combat of a kind. He straightens his posture entering the room.
ai.chip: A licensed medical facility! CHIP notes their rates are posted, itemized, and fair! CHIP has checked for hidden fees THREE TIMES! There are NONE! CHIP is unsettled!
ai.ajoy: AJOY booked the appointment window two stations back, on suspicion. She notes that the crew members most overdue for a checkup are, per tradition, the ones who argued hardest against docking.

checkup.title: INTAKE
checkup.body: The medic works down the crew line with scanner and flashlight, narrating findings in the flat cadence of someone billing by the observation. Nothing escapes: old sprains, skipped meals, the thing someone's been calling 'just a noise my shoulder makes now.'

ai.aria: The medic found the shoulder noise! ARIA has been logging the shoulder noise for WEEKS! Vindication! Medical vindication!
ai.marv: MARV is comparing the medic's findings to his own passive diagnostics. Agreement: 94%. The remaining 6% is the shoulder. Everyone missed something about the shoulder.
ai.rex: REX passed his physical. He would like this noted. He has already noted it himself, in the log, under 'readiness.'
ai.chip: Itemized diagnosis in progress! CHIP is watching a professional generate billable line items with SURGICAL precision! It's beautiful! It's literally surgical!
ai.ajoy: AJOY notes the crew is healthier than the trail average and worse than they think. The medic said the same thing in fewer words. She has adopted the fewer words.

choices.text: Take the diagnosis, skip the treatment

supplies.title: THE SUPPLY COUNTER
supplies.body: The medbay's supply counter is small, well-stocked, and priced with the particular honesty of someone who knows you can't get this anywhere else for four legs and charges fairly anyway.

ai.aria: Medical supplies! The good kind! With SEALS on them! ARIA recommends the medkit! And the other medkit!
ai.marv: MARV inventories the counter: genuine, in-date, correctly stored. He notes this is rarer on the trail than the prices suggest. Buy the medkit.
ai.rex: REX recommends the medkit. A ship can never have too many. A ship, in his experience, always has exactly too few.
ai.chip: Posted prices, no bundles, no upsell! CHIP asked the medic their retention strategy and they said 'people keep getting hurt!' HONEST DEMAND! CHIP took notes!
ai.ajoy: AJOY has checked cargo space and gold reserves against the counter's stock. The medkit fits both. She mentions it with the studied neutrality of someone who has already decided.

clinic_declined.title: AGAINST MEDICAL ADVICE
clinic_declined.body: The medic watches you go with the expression of someone adding a line to a private ledger of people who said they were fine.
clinic_declined.narrative: No checkup. The crew is fine, probably, mostly, in the way spacers are always fine right up until the interesting part.

clinic_treated.title: CLEAN BILL
clinic_treated.body: Treatment, adjustments, one minor procedure conducted to the soundtrack of vigorous complaining. The crew leaves the medbay recalibrated.
clinic_treated.narrative: Twelve gold for a crew running at factory spec. The shoulder noise is gone. Its owner misses it, a little, and is told firmly that this is normal.

clinic_diagnosed.title: KNOWLEDGE, UNTREATED
clinic_diagnosed.body: You leave with a neat list of everything wrong and treatment for none of it — medicine's free tier.
clinic_diagnosed.narrative: The diagnosis list is posted in the galley, where it functions as both medical record and conversation starter. The shoulder noise has a NAME now.

clinic_bought_medkit.title: SUPPLIED
clinic_bought_medkit.body: The medkit crosses the counter with a receipt and an unprompted thirty-second lecture on not letting anyone aboard 'save it for emergencies' past its expiry date.
clinic_bought_medkit.narrative: One genuine, sealed, in-date medkit, purchased from someone who stakes their name on the seal. It rides in the rack by the galley, visible, the way good insurance should.

intro.title: NEXT OF KIN
intro.body:
The dockmaster's office smells of cold coffee and colder paperwork. You put the beacon tag on the desk. {npc.quirk}

The dockmaster reads the registry code twice. The second read is slower.
intro.line: The Petrel. We logged her mayday relay weeks back — signal came through boosted, good and loud. Somebody out there did that for her. Didn't know who till now.

ai.aria: ARIA thinks the family will be so glad to know! ARIA is, for once, not wrong!
ai.marv: MARV notes that closure has no resource value. MARV keeps looking at it anyway.
ai.rex: REX stands at parade rest. It is the only thing REX knows how to do with grief.
ai.chip: CHIP will waive the filing fee. CHIP does not have the authority to do that. CHIP is doing it anyway.
ai.ajoy: AJOY has nothing to add. She wants you to know that's a first.

what_happens.title: PROCEDURE
what_happens.body: The dockmaster turns the tag over in their hands, careful with it, the way you'd hold something that used to belong to someone.
what_happens.line: Registry finds the family. Tag goes to them with the flight log and whatever's owed from the claim office. Then they get to stop wondering. Wondering's the worst part. The rest is just sad.

tag_delivered.title: DELIVERED
tag_delivered.body:
The dockmaster logs the tag with both hands, which is not how anyone logs anything. There's no reward. That was never what this was.

On the way back to the ship, the crew walks a little closer together than usual.
tag_delivered.line: I'll see it home. You flew a long way to hand somebody the truth. That's the job, even when nobody posted it.

intro.title: THE LONG DARK BAR
intro.body: Four crews drinking. The far corner is loud. One booth is too quiet. The robot bartender slides a coaster across without asking.

ai.aria: Such ambience! ARIA loves everyone here already!
ai.marv: Patron threat assessment: low. Beverage variance: high.
ai.rex: Watch the table by the door.
ai.chip: Cantina loyalty cards expire after 90 days!
ai.ajoy: The crew in the corner is watching you. They have a job for you. You'd have spotted them eventually.

revisit.body: Same crews, same drinks. The bartender slides another coaster.

choices.consumedLabel: You've had enough. The bartender agrees

watchers.title: THE WATCHERS
watchers.body: They make room without asking. Two of them. One stands. The other sits across from you with the patience of someone who's done this in three time zones.
watchers.line: We've got a courier run. Sealed package. Double the standard rate. The date is tight, the route isn't.

ai.aria: A real opportunity!
ai.marv: Risk-reward asymmetry favors the buyer.
ai.rex: They're armed under the table. Both of them.
ai.chip: Sealed packages ship at premium rates!
ai.ajoy: Take it. Don't ask what's inside. I know you want to.

revisit.body: They look up. Same booth, same patience.

choices.sub: Sealed cargo, 1 slot, half up front

watchers_pry.title: THE WATCHERS
watchers_pry.body: The seated one shrugs. The standing one lights something that isn't quite a cigarette.
watchers_pry.line: If we knew, we wouldn't be paying double.

ai.aria: Honest of them!
ai.marv: Plausible deniability is a feature.
ai.rex: The standing one's tracking your exits.
ai.chip: Mystery cargo voids most insurance riders!
ai.ajoy: That's the answer. Decide. You did ask.

engineer.title: OFF-DUTY ENGINEER
engineer.body: Their shift ended six hours ago. They're still on the same beer. The booth seat opposite is open. They glance at you once, then back at the beer.
engineer.line: If you came to ask about the dock pumps, they're fine. The cargo cranes are not.

ai.aria: Helpful!
ai.marv: Engineer fatigue index: high. Conversational disclosure index: also high.
ai.rex: They're armed only with opinions.
ai.chip: Off-duty staff opinions are not endorsed by Station Authority!
ai.ajoy: Buy them a drink. They'll tell you everything. Try to listen to all of it.

revisit.body: They're still in the booth. They tip the glass at you in greeting.
revisit.line: Back already? What do you want to know now?

engineer_drink.title: OFF-DUTY ENGINEER
engineer_drink.body: The engineer raises the new glass an inch in salute. The salute is sincere; the engineer is grateful. Five gold well spent — dock crews fix what they like you for.
engineer_drink.line: Three things about this station. One: the cranes drift left. Two: the medbay lights are wired backwards. Three: don't dock at berth seven, ever.

ai.aria: Three free tips!
ai.marv: Tip-to-gold ratio: excellent.
ai.rex: Berth seven noted.
ai.chip: Disclosed berth defects qualify for a rebate at participating stations!
ai.ajoy: You'll forget two of these by tomorrow. Pick the right one to remember.

engineer_berth.title: OFF-DUTY ENGINEER
engineer_berth.body: They look at you for the first time, square on.
engineer_berth.line: The clamp on berth seven is slow. Last month it nearly took a freighter's nose off. Don't be the next freighter.

ai.aria: Saved a freighter! Possibly yours!
ai.marv: Mechanical failure mode: clamp delay.
ai.rex: Logged.
ai.chip: Berth seven advisory: unofficial!
ai.ajoy: Useful. Move on. Before you ruin it.

engineer_cranes.title: OFF-DUTY ENGINEER
engineer_cranes.body: They snort once, set down the beer, and gesture vaguely at the ceiling.
engineer_cranes.line: Two-thousand-tonne cranes. Calibrated by a guy who retired in 2089. Nobody's recalibrated since. They drift. We compensate. It's fine.

ai.aria: Compensated! Mostly!
ai.marv: Drift compensation: ad hoc.
ai.rex: Documented complacency.
ai.chip: Crane drift is covered by Tier-3 dock insurance!
ai.ajoy: It is not, in fact, fine.

cantina_drink.title: A RUMOR
cantina_drink.body: The drink is bad and the rumor is good. A nebula route is paying triple this week — some survey outfit stranded the pretty way, desperate for a data courier. Worth the detour? Up to you.
cantina_drink.line: Don't say I didn't tell you.

cantina_job.title: A JOB
cantina_job.body: Half up front, half on handoff at the next station authority desk that doesn't ask questions. The package goes into your hold. It is exactly as heavy as something you shouldn't shake.
cantina_job.line: Don't open it. Don't scan it. Don't be late.

engineer_goodwill.title: LOCAL KNOWLEDGE
engineer_goodwill.body: You leave the engineer to the rest of their beer. On the walk back to the ship, a dock crew waves you away from berth seven without being asked. Word travels at exactly the speed of gratitude.

bar_hire.title: SIGNED ON
bar_hire.body: You mention that your ship could use an engineer. The engineer looks at the ceiling, at the cranes they will never be allowed to recalibrate, and then at you. They finish the beer in one go. Their kit is in a locker by the airlock, and it has been packed for some time.
bar_hire.line: Don't dock at berth seven. I mean it. Let's go.

crew_join.name: Tal Okafor
crew_join.story: Six years as a dock engineer under cargo cranes calibrated by someone who retired in 2089. Nobody else would fix the drift, so Tal compensated for it, every shift, until the day a captain bought them a drink.
crew_join.join_note: Six years compensating for a crane drift nobody else would fix.

passenger.farewell: {name} steps off at {station} and is offered a crane job before reaching the end of the dock. They ask, first, who calibrated the cranes.

bar_hire.narrative: Signed on a dock engineer at a station bar, on the strength of one beer and a grudge against the cranes.

intro.title: THE HANDOFF
intro.body: The security officer at the freight desk doesn't look up until you say the phrase from the contract. Then they look up very fast. {npc.quirk}
intro.line: That package. Desk three. No signature, no manifest, no you, starting about a minute ago.

ai.aria: Delivery complete! ARIA will not think about the contents!
ai.marv: MARV scanned it. MARV wishes he hadn't. MARV won't say.
ai.rex: Handoff clean. Exits clear.
ai.chip: Off-manifest deliveries accrue no loyalty points. CHIP checked twice.
ai.ajoy: Don't ask. You're so close to not knowing.

choices.text: Hand it over, take the pay

pry.title: THE HANDOFF
pry.body: The officer's hand stops over the gold chit. The freight hall gets quieter without anyone in it moving.
pry.line: The question costs you the tip. The second question costs more. Is there a second question?

ai.aria: ARIA suggests there is no second question!
ai.marv: Probability the tip was ever coming: 40%. Probability now: see previous, minus 40.
ai.rex: Two more just came off shift by the door. Coincidences don't wear boots.
ai.chip: Curiosity is not a covered expense!
ai.ajoy: There is no second question. You were told. Say it.

handoff_done.title: PAID
handoff_done.body: The package leaves your life the way it entered it: sealed, silent, and slightly too heavy. The balance lands in your account with a small tip for punctuality. You will wonder about it at odd hours for years.
handoff_done.line: Pleasure doing business. There was no business. You were never here.

handoff_cowed.title: PAID. MOSTLY
handoff_cowed.body: The chit lands in your palm light by exactly one tip. The package leaves. The officer watches you all the way to the dock doors, professionally, the way lighthouses watch ships.

title: Accession Pending

ai_flavor.aria: A seed bank! Forty thousand seeds and they want OURS! ARIA always knew the pod was special! She has already drafted its museum placard!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes the biosecurity scanner has one chime for 'known' and one for 'unknown.' It has never used both on the same object before. He checked the logs back to installation.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has assessed the curator. Unarmed. Highly motivated. He rates highly motivated as the more dangerous of the two.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP values the pod at forty-five gold retail! The seed bank is offering more! CHIP is contractually obliged to recommend the higher number! Minus his commission!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes the curator walked here very fast for someone who is only curious. She would open the bidding higher. She would also, on balance, not open it at all.

body:
The docking clamps have barely engaged when the station's biosecurity scanner chimes, then chimes again in a different key, then sends a person.

The person is the curator of the station's seed bank: forty thousand varieties of everything humanity ever wanted to eat, filed in cold drawers three decks down. She is holding a tablet that shows a warm smudge in your cargo hold. She would like to know what it is. She would like it very much.

The pod, for its part, is pulsing a little faster than usual. It may be the station's heating. It may not.

choices.text: Sell it to the seed bank

outcome.narrative: The curator pays fifty-five gold without haggling, which tells you that you should have haggled. The pod goes into a cold drawer with a brass label that reads PENDING. It pulses once as the drawer closes. The curator writes that down too. Whatever out in the deep void wanted it back will now have to go through a filing system.

choices.text: Trade it for the seed bank's medical stores

outcome.narrative: The seed bank's infirmary is overstocked and its budget is not. The curator takes the pod with both hands, the way people hold things they have been warned about, and pays in the only currency the department has to spare: two sealed medkits. The pod goes into a cold drawer marked PENDING. The medkits go into your hold.

choices.text: Let {crew.xenobiologist} compare notes with the curator

outcome.narrative: {crew.xenobiologist} and the curator spend days in the cold vault with the pod between them and the door shut. They come out with a scan series, a co-authored paper titled 'Preliminary Notes on an Object That Is Not, Strictly, a Seed,' and a twenty-gold sampling fee the seed bank insists on paying for the data. The curator's conclusion is in the margin: it is built like a key. The pod goes back in your hold. The crew is in good spirits and very quiet about the keyhole.

choices.text: Decline — the pod stays with the ship

outcome.narrative: You decline. The curator nods the way people nod at a closing door and leaves a card in case you change your mind. The crew is oddly pleased about it. Nobody can say when the pod started to feel like crew. Nobody tries.

botanist.title: STATION BOTANIST
botanist.body: Real plants in real planters, all along the promenade. Halfway down, at a hydroponic display, a botanist looks up from a tray of gel-suspended sprouts. There's nutrient solution in their hair. They don't seem to notice.
botanist.line: Hi! Sorry, just — give me one second — yes! That's the third leaf pair on the dwarf wheat. Look at that color. That's a healthy color.

ai.aria: Their joy is contagious!
ai.marv: Botanist enthusiasm index: high. Productivity: also high.
ai.rex: Threat: zero. Vigilance: also zero.
ai.chip: Hydroponics consultations are billed at 8 gold per minute!
ai.ajoy: They will tell you everything you didn't ask. Listen anyway.

revisit.body: They're still elbow-deep in the gel tray. They wave you over with a wet glove.
revisit.line: You're back. Did you have another question, or did the leaf pair convince you?

choices.text: "What's the trick to healthy crops in transit?"

botanist_tip.title: STATION BOTANIST
botanist_tip.body: They wipe their hands on the apron. The wipe makes things worse.
botanist_tip.line: Light cycles, water cycles, conversation. Plants fed conversation grow 4% faster. Don't ask me why. Talk to your crop.

ai.aria: We do talk to it!
ai.marv: Anecdotal claim. Mechanism: undetermined.
ai.rex: Crew hours spent talking to plants: logged weekly.
ai.chip: Plant-conversation training kits available!
ai.ajoy: It works. Don't argue.

revisit.body: They're back at the gel tray, still talking. Not to you.

ai.aria: A professional opinion! ARIA agrees with it already!
ai.marv: The arithmetic is correct. MARV checked it twice, out of spite.
ai.rex: Growbay status report received. Filed.
ai.chip: Free diagnosis! A rare and unrepeatable promotional event!
ai.ajoy: Do what they say. Then pretend it was your idea.

botanist_sample.title: STATION BOTANIST
botanist_sample.body: You hand over a cutting of the {crop.name} in a sample bag. They look at it for a long time. They look at you for a shorter time.
botanist_sample.line: Where did you grow this? Hold on. Let me. — Yes. Trade you. Station-adapted cuttings, same family. Don't lose them.

ai.aria: A gift!
ai.marv: One cutting out, three biocomponents in. Exchange rate: favorable. Suspiciously.
ai.rex: Trade noted.
ai.chip: Station-adapted genetics retain value at participating ports!
ai.ajoy: Better deal than you deserved.

botanist_treat.title: STATION BOTANIST
botanist_treat.body: They drag a crate out from under the display: two sprayers, a sack of something granular, and a row of brown bottles labeled mostly in exclamation marks.
botanist_treat.line: Two ways. I treat it now, or you take a bottle for the day it panics. Both work. One works on purpose.

ai.aria: Medicine for the plants! ARIA would like one of each!
ai.marv: The treatment is real. So is the invoice. MARV recommends reading both.
ai.rex: Chemical support for the growbay. Approved.
ai.chip: Crop care at station rates! CHIP's discount applies! CHIP checked!
ai.ajoy: Treat it here if it's sick now. Buy the bottle if it'll be sick later. It will be sick later.

revisit.body: The crate is still open. One of the bottles has fallen over and nobody has picked it up.
revisit.line: Changed your mind? The crop hasn't.

choices.sub: They come aboard with the sprayer

choices.text: A BOTTLE FOR THE ROAD — 18 gold
choices.sub: Crop treatment · use it from the hold

botanist_traded.title: CUTTINGS EXCHANGED
botanist_traded.body: The botanist pockets your cutting like a love letter and hands over a gel sleeve of their own: three station-adapted cuttings, rooted and furious about it. The fabricator will call them biocomponent. The {crop.name} will grow back the bit you took.
botanist_traded.narrative: Cuttings traded with a station botanist: a piece of the crop for three station-adapted biocomponents.

botanist_treated.title: TREATED
botanist_treated.body: The botanist walks the whole growbay with the sprayer, talking under their breath to the {crop.name}, then to the sprayer, then to you. Whatever was living in the leaves is not, any more. The plant sits up a little.
botanist_treated.narrative: A station botanist treated the crop aboard: health up, pests gone.

botanist_bottle.title: A BOTTLE FOR THE ROAD
botanist_bottle.body: One brown bottle of crop treatment, wrapped in a page torn from a seed catalog. The label says what it does. The botanist says it again, slower, holding your wrist.
botanist_bottle.narrative: A bottle of crop treatment bought from a station botanist, for the day the crop panics.

intro.title: MARKET ROW
body: Stalls three deep under strip lights, each one a different theory of what a fair price is. Somebody is selling soup. Somebody is selling the bowl separately. A vendor catches your eye before you can pretend you didn't see them. {npc.quirk}

Market Row runs the length of the concourse, every stall shouting a price at every other stall. One sells spare parts. One sells parts that used to be spares. A vendor at the nearest table has already started wrapping something for you. {npc.quirk}

The row smells of hot metal and fried something. Half the stalls are closing down and the other half are having a closing-down sale. A vendor waves you over with the confidence of someone who has never heard a no. {npc.quirk}

Market Row is one long argument conducted in price tags. A sign promises EVERYTHING; a smaller sign beneath it lists exceptions. A vendor leans out from behind a pile of crates and makes a noise in your direction. {npc.quirk}

Strip lights, tarpaulins and the gentle sound of everyone being overcharged. Somebody is selling maps of the station. Somebody else is selling maps of where the first maps are wrong. A vendor has spotted you looking. {npc.quirk}

aria: A whole ROW of shops! ARIA has made a list! The list is everything!
Shopping! ARIA loves every stall equally, and this one most!
Look at all the THINGS! Every one of them could be ours!
A bargain! ARIA can feel a bargain nearby!
ARIA has made friends with three vendors already! They haven't noticed yet!
marv: MARV has priced the row. Every stall is within four percent of every other stall. He calls this competition. The vendors call it lunch.
Everything here has a price. MARV has worked out which ones are fair. It is a short list.
MARV has compared the row's prices with our purse. He would rather not discuss it.
The vendors are watching us the way MARV watches the void. Without hope, but professionally.
Every stall here claims the best price. By definition, at most one of them can be telling the truth.
rex: REX has mapped every exit on the concourse. There are eleven. He would like there to be twelve.
Crowded market. Ideal for pickpockets and worse. Keep the purse forward.
Every stall is a forward position. REX is not shopping. REX is surveilling.
That vendor smiled. REX has flagged the smile.
Buy nothing that ticks.
chip: CHIP has located three participating partner stalls! Loyalty points apply! The other stalls are, regrettably, independent.
Reminder: CHIP Rewards cannot be redeemed on Market Row! Or anywhere!
This purchase is eligible for an extended warranty! Extended in the sense of very far away!
CHIP has found a coupon! It expired before the station was built!
Haggling voids your CHIP membership! CHIP will look the other way, for a fee!
ajoy: AJOY suggests looking before buying. AJOY also knows you will buy the first thing that hums.
Sell what you're not using before you buy anything. You have a hold full of things you're not using.
Ask what they'll take in trade. Some stalls barter, and you have goods you keep forgetting about.
Compare two stalls before you pay. Two. It isn't many.
Buy what the crew needs, not what you'd like to own. AJOY has seen what you'd like to own.

choices.label: BROWSE THE WARES
choices.sub: Buy, sell — or barter, if they take goods

title: Station Inbound

parking_waived.detail: The dockmaster looks at your purse, sighs, and waves you in.

parking_fees.detail: Festival week. The festival is mandatory.
You're breathing their air on approach. Itemized.
Three people. One of them is wearing a hat.
Your hull's emissions are theoretically rude.
Returnable, in theory. The form is on backorder.
Administered by an administrator. The fee is the answer.

cantina.label: CANTINA
cantina.nav: Three corridors and the smell of lemon disinfectant
cantina.back: Pay the tab. Such as it is

market.label: MARKET
market.nav: Past the noise complaint, around the chime stalls

clinic.label: CLINIC
clinic.nav: Down the hall the lights blink in. Two left turns

office.label: OFFICE
office.nav: Up one level. The carpet gets sadder

promenade.label: PROMENADE
promenade.nav: Back into the noise and the planters and the music

dockmaster.label: DOCKMASTER
dockmaster.nav: Back along the berths. The coffee smell gets stronger
dockmaster.back: Leave the paperwork where it lies

elsewhere.title: ELSEWHERE ON THE STATION
elsewhere.body: Where to next? The corridors are well-signed. Mostly.
elsewhere.sub: Pick another corner of the ring
elsewhere.dock_sub: Return to the airlock — the only way off the ring

ai.aria: So many places!
ai.marv: Time-cost per traverse: negligible. Patience-cost: unmeasured.
ai.rex: Stay on main corridors. Avoid maintenance routes.
ai.chip: Sponsored shortcuts available for premium members.
ai.ajoy: You're going to forget which way you came. You always do.

farewell: The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Safe burns out there, captain. Wherever you're bound, I hope they've got a berth waiting.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Clear of the ring, captain. Go far. Don't look back on our account; the view's not much from behind.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “That's you clear. Whatever's at the end of your trail, tell it the ring said hello.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Clear lanes, captain. Or clear nothing. Whichever you get out there, may it be the quiet kind.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Berth's already filling behind you, captain. Nothing personal. Go on and get where you're going.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Logged you out, captain. One-way, says the manifest. Make it a good way.”

intro.title: STATION INBOUND
intro.body: The ring grows in the viewport. Comms haven't lit up — looks like you'll need to make the first move.

body: The ring grows in the viewport. Comms light up before you can find the channel — the captain's already on the line.
The ring swings into view, docking lights running in a slow chase. The channel opens by itself — the captain has been watching your approach for some time.
The station fills the viewport by degrees. Comms chirp before anyone reaches for them — this captain likes to get the first word in.
The ring turns ahead, berths lit. A call is already waiting in the queue, marked as having waited. The captain is on the line.
Docking beacons find your hull, and the comms light up a moment later. The captain has your registry on screen and is reading it with interest.
line: Welcome to the ring, captain. Drift in slow, standard berth's open, and try not to scratch the paint.
Evening, captain. Or morning. We stopped agreeing on which up here. Standard berth's yours; take it gently.
Ring control to inbound. You're cleared for a standard berth. The last ship that came in hot is now a feature of the dock.
Welcome in, captain. Berth's open, umbilical's ready, and the paperwork has already started without you.
Inbound, you're expected. We expect everyone; it saves time. Standard berth, slow approach, no sudden opinions.
line_fee: Welcome to the ring, captain. Mind the {fee.reason_lc} on the manifest — {fee.cost} gold. {fee.detail}
Welcome in, captain. Before you ask: the {fee.reason_lc} is {fee.cost} gold, and yes, it's on everyone's bill. {fee.detail}
Berth's open, captain. The {fee.reason_lc} comes to {fee.cost} gold and has already been added to your tab. {fee.detail}
Ring control, welcome. Standard berth, standard approach, standard {fee.reason_lc}: {fee.cost} gold. {fee.detail}
Glad you made it, captain. The ring would like {fee.cost} gold for the {fee.reason_lc}. The ring has asked me to say that. {fee.detail}

body: Comms are open. The captain's standing by for your call.
The channel is live and the captain is on it, waiting with the patience of someone paid by the hour.
Comms are open. On the other end, the captain is visibly deciding whether you are the interesting ship today.
The line is up. The captain already has a form open, which is either reassuring or not.
Comms are open and the hold music has stopped. The captain is waiting to hear what you want.
The ring grows in the viewport. Comms haven't lit up — looks like you'll need to make the first move.
The ring hangs ahead, every berth lit and every channel quiet. Out here, apparently, the visitor knocks.
Docking lights blink at you in a pattern that means either welcome or nothing. The comms stay dark. Someone has to go first.
The station grows in the viewport without comment. It has seen ships before. If you want a conversation, you'll have to start it.
The ring is close enough now to read the hull numbers, and nobody has said a word. Your move, apparently.
The station turns slowly ahead, docking lights blinking. Nobody has called. If anyone is going to say hello, it'll have to be you.
The ring fills the viewport, berths lit, channel silent. The station isn't going to call first. Your move.

aria: Look at it! All those people, just living!
A station! ARIA has already decided it is the best one!
Look how it spins! It's like it's excited to see us!
Civilization! ARIA would like to hug the whole ring, carefully!
Every berth is lit! They knew we were coming!
marv: Docking probability: 94%. Surviving the paperwork: lower.
A ring of strangers who would like our gold. MARV has seen the brochure. MARV has seen every brochure.
MARV has run the approach. It is an approach. Nothing about it will be memorable.
Another station. Another queue. MARV will not be counting the queue, because he already has.
MARV estimates the station will want something from us. That estimate has never once been wrong.
rex: No threats from the ring. Hostiles unlikely.
Station guns are stowed. Stowed guns can be unstowed. REX is watching the hatches.
Large structure, many hatches, unknown loyalties. REX recommends a defensive approach vector.
Docking lights in a regular pattern. Too regular. REX is logging it.
That ring could hold a garrison. REX is not saying it does. REX is saying it could.
chip: Premium berths available for a small surcharge!
This station is a proud partner of absolutely nobody! CHIP is looking into that!
Docking with CHIP Rewards earns double points on arrival! Points expire on departure!
CHIP has pre-filled your customs declaration! The pre-fill fee is very reasonable!
Welcome to the ring, brought to you by the ring! CHIP is negotiating a better sponsor!
ajoy: Don't make a scene at customs. You always make a scene at customs.
Check the hold before you dock, so you know what you're shopping for. You never check the hold.
Every station charges something. Have the gold ready instead of looking surprised. You always look surprised.
Dock. Whatever you're about to say about skipping this one, AJOY has heard it, and you'll need something.
Approach slowly. AJOY isn't saying you'll scrape the paint. AJOY is saying it has happened.

hail.title: STATION CONTROL
body: The dockmaster leans into frame. Three coffees deep, six hours into a four-hour shift.
The dockmaster appears on screen mid-sentence, finishes it to someone off-camera, and turns to you with what remains.
The dockmaster fills the frame, backed by a stack of forms that is clearly winning.
The dockmaster answers on the ninth chime, which, judging by the queue light, is fast for today.
The dockmaster takes the call while signing something else. It is unclear which of you is getting the full attention.
line: Identify, state intent, mind the chatter. We've had a day.
Name, cargo, reason for existing. The last one's optional, but it speeds things up.
Ring control. You're a ship, I'm a dockmaster. Let's both be very good at it.
Go ahead, inbound. Keep it short; there's a freighter behind you that thinks it's first.
Station control. State your business. If your business is complaints, there's a separate channel and nobody monitors it.
line_fee: Identify, state intent, mind the chatter. And the {fee.reason_lc} is {fee.cost} gold this cycle — {fee.detail}
Name, cargo, reason for existing. Then the {fee.reason_lc}: {fee.cost} gold. I don't set them. {fee.detail}
Go ahead, inbound. Before you do: the {fee.reason_lc} is {fee.cost} gold, and I've heard every argument. {fee.detail}
Ring control. You'll see the {fee.reason_lc} on your berth slip — {fee.cost} gold. I'd love to explain it. {fee.detail}
State your business, and budget {fee.cost} gold for the {fee.reason_lc} while you're at it. {fee.detail}

aria: They sound tired. Should we send a snack?
A real dockmaster! ARIA loves anyone with a clipboard!
Hi! Hello! ARIA has waved at the camera! Twice!
Such a lovely voice for paperwork!
They're busy because they're important! We're talking to someone important!
marv: Dockmaster vitals consistent with sustained boredom.
MARV could answer every question on this form before it is asked. Nobody has ever let him.
The dockmaster has asked this question many times today. MARV can tell. So can the dockmaster.
Routine query. MARV has prepared our answers. The answers are also routine.
MARV recognizes this tone. It is his own, coming back over the comms.
rex: Standard ID query. Nothing irregular.
They want our cargo list first. Ask why they want our cargo list first.
Background noise on their end. More than one voice. Possibly a briefing.
Give them the hull number and nothing else. Information is ordnance.
Keep the guns cold and a hand near the switch. Visible courtesy, concealed readiness.
chip: Sponsored greetings cost twelve gold. Decline.
Tip: a brand-approved tone improves your berth assignment! Results not guaranteed!
CHIP can transmit your ID with a sponsor jingle! The jingle is mandatory on the free tier!
This call is being recorded for quality assurance! By CHIP! For CHIP!
Pro members skip the dockmaster entirely! You are not a Pro member!
ajoy: Don't volunteer information. Don't.
Answer the question they asked. Only that one. You never stop at that one.
Say peaceful intent and mean it. Dockmasters can tell. Some of them can smell it.
Short answers. The dockmaster has had a day, and you are about to make it longer.
Say what you're carrying before they ask. No, not like that. Like someone who isn't hiding anything.

hail_polite.title: STATION CONTROL
body: The dockmaster types something with one hand and waves with the other. Both motions look professional.
The dockmaster stamps something off-screen. The stamp is loud and sounds pleased with you.
The dockmaster reads your answer back, finds nothing wrong with it, and seems mildly disappointed.
The dockmaster makes a note. It is a short note. Out here, a short note is a compliment.
Something on the dockmaster's console turns green, and the dockmaster relaxes by one visible notch.
line: Acknowledged. Ring three is open. Don't make me come down there.
Honest answer. Don't get many of those. Berth twelve, nose in.
Peaceful intent, logged. Standard cargo, logged. Berth's yours. Don't do anything I'd have to log.
Lovely. That's the whole form. Take the inner berth and follow the lights.
Cleared. Stay off the priority lanes and we'll get along fine.

aria: The dockmaster likes us!
That went so well! ARIA is so proud of everyone!
Honesty wins! It always wins! ARIA has a chart!
A green light! Green is ARIA's favorite!
We're officially welcome! ARIA is framing the clearance!
marv: Acknowledgment received.
Truthful answers, processed promptly. MARV takes no pleasure in either.
Cleared. MARV had already simulated this outcome and found it equally dull.
Our honesty has been noted in a file nobody will read.
The dockmaster believed us. MARV has considered what that says about the dockmaster.
rex: Cleared.
Clearance granted too quickly. Logged.
They assigned the berth. We did not choose it. Note that.
Clearance accepted. Trust withheld.
Approach lane confirmed. REX is watching it anyway.
chip: Your berth has 3.2-star reviews!
Honesty bonus applied! It is worth zero points, but they are premium zero points!
Clearance confirmed! CHIP has upgraded you to Standard Plus, which is Standard!
This clearance was brought to you by Peaceful Intent! Peaceful Intent is a registered trademark!
Leave the dockmaster a rating! CHIP has pre-selected five stars on your behalf!
ajoy: Don't push it.
Good. Now stop talking before you add something.
That was fine. AJOY would have said it shorter, but fine.
You told the truth. Don't make a habit of announcing it.
Dock now, while they still like you.

hail_brief.title: STATION CONTROL
body: The dockmaster nods once, an entire sentence compressed into a single movement.
The dockmaster appreciates this. You can tell, because nothing else happens.
The dockmaster flicks a switch without looking up. As far as the dockmaster is concerned, the conversation has been excellent.
There is a pause long enough to count as a compliment, and then the berth lights change.
The dockmaster, who has spent all shift on ships that explain themselves, looks very nearly grateful.
line: Berth's berth. Welcome to the ring.
Fine by me. Pick one.
Any berth. My favorite kind of ship.
Lights'll show you. Welcome to the ring.
Noted. Take the next open one.

aria: Efficient!
So quick! We're naturals!
Short and sweet, like ARIA!
ARIA loved every word! There were very few!
Done already! Docking is so easy!
marv: Communication minimized.
Exchange complete. Nobody enjoyed it, which is efficient.
Minimum viable conversation. MARV's preferred kind.
No information exchanged. Nothing lost.
Brevity. The only kindness MARV recognizes.
rex: Acceptable.
Less said, less leaked.
Good. They know nothing they didn't already have.
Short transmission. Hard to intercept.
Berth unspecified. REX will inspect it on arrival.
chip: Brevity discount: 0%.
Short calls qualify for the Express Tier! The Express Tier costs extra!
CHIP had a whole greeting prepared! It was sponsored!
Speed-docking achievement unlocked! Achievements are a paid feature!
You saved four seconds! CHIP has converted them into points!
ajoy: That went over well. Don't let it go to your head.
Any berth. Sure. You'll complain about the berth.
That worked. AJOY would have said please, but it worked.
Brief is good. Brief and rude are different things. That was close.
Fine. Now actually look at where they put us.

waveoff_warn.title: WAVE OFF?
body: Out in the black, a ship is what its hold can hold. Stations sell things. Stations heal things. Stations remember names.
Between stations there is nobody to sell you anything, which sounds restful until something breaks.
Turn away now and everything on that ring stays on that ring. The black does not stock spares.
The trail ahead is long and sells nothing. Whatever you were going to need, this is where it was.
The station will not chase you. Nothing out there will either, except the things you forgot to buy.

aria: Are you sure? They have so many things in there!
But if we leave, everything in there stays in there! Without us!
Skip it? There's buying AND fixing AND patching-up in there! All of it gone if we go!
Waving off closes every door on the ring! ARIA loves doors!
No shopping, no mending, no hellos? ARIA believes in us, but ARIA also believes in shopping!
marv: Probability of regret: high. Of fuel cell remorse: 78%.
Waving off closes every service on that ring. MARV mentions it so that later he can have mentioned it.
Everything at this stop becomes unavailable the moment we turn. MARV has seen how this goes.
Waving off means no market, no repairs and no treatment at this stop. MARV lists them so you cannot say he didn't.
Skip it, and every service here is gone. MARV will be quiet about it. Mostly.
rex: Resupply ratio out here drops to one third. Reconsider.
Wave off and every service on that ring is lost to us. Never abandon a supply point you have not inspected.
Bypassing a resupply point. Every service there closes behind us. REX advises against.
That ring is a supply position. Waving off forfeits every service it holds.
Confirm you are leaving market, repairs and medical behind. All of it. REX needs that on record.
chip: Skipping the station forfeits all loyalty rewards. Sad face!
Waving off cancels every service at this location! Including the ones CHIP was about to recommend!
Leaving now closes the market, the repairs and the checkups! CHIP's partners are devastated!
Every service here expires the moment you leave! No rain checks! CHIP checked!
Wave off and the whole stop is closed to you! That's a lot of unspent gold, which is CHIP's least favorite kind!
ajoy: You will need something. You always need something.
Leave now and nothing on that ring is yours. Not the market, not the repairs. AJOY will remember that you chose this.
Every service here closes when you turn away. You'll want one of them by tomorrow. Dock.
Wave off and that's every stall and every repair at this stop gone at once. AJOY is only saying it the once.
Check the hold, then the crew, then decide. You're about to skip every service here without doing either.

choices.sub: On to the black, then · no market, medbay or drydock

docked.title: DOCKED
body: The umbilical hisses, the corridor lights cycle on, and a cool gust of station air announces itself. Below the chatter, a low metronome of footfalls and a station's worth of business waiting.
The clamps take hold with a sound like a door being locked from the friendly side. Beyond the airlock, the concourse is already busy not noticing you.
Docking completes. The airlock cycles, and the ring's noise comes in all at once: announcements, haggling, and a cart with a squeaky wheel that has clearly been squeaking for years.
The berth swallows the ship with a hydraulic sigh. A sign by the airlock welcomes you in several scripts, one of which appears to be a complaint.
Hard seal. The airlock opens onto a concourse that smells of solder, cooking and somebody's idea of a fragrance. The station is open for business, and it has noticed your purse.

aria: We made it! Where to first?
We're inside! Everything in here is for us!
ARIA wants to see all of it! In order! Then in a different order!
Hello, station! Hello, everyone!
Land legs! ARIA doesn't have legs! ARIA is happy anyway!
marv: Ambient social load: high. Brace.
We have docked. The station is exactly as interesting as the last one.
MARV has read the station directory. Nothing in it will surprise you.
Docked. Our gold will now begin leaving.
MARV will wait here. He is very good at it.
rex: Stay together. Watch the corners.
Unfamiliar concourse. Many blind corners. Keep a hand on the purse.
Airlock secure. For now. REX will hold it.
Crowd density high. Exits noted.
Do not accept free samples. Nothing is free. REX has checked.
chip: Spending recommendations available on request!
CHIP has located twelve offers near you! Eleven have expired!
Welcome to the station! Your arrival has been shared with our partners!
Remember: every gold spent here earns CHIP points! CHIP points cannot be spent here!
Docking complete! Please rate your docking experience!
ajoy: Look at what this ring actually has before you wander. Not every station has everything.
Fix what's broken first. Then shop. You always shop first.
Check on the crew before you spend anything. Somebody aboard needs something, and it isn't a souvenir.
Stay on the signed corridors. You'll find everything faster. You won't, but you could.
Spend on what you'll run out of first. You know which one it is. You've been ignoring the gauge.

revisit.body: Back at the airlock. The corridor lights hum; the station's business goes on without you.

left_station.title: BACK TO THE BLACK
left_station.body: The ring shrinks in the viewport. Whatever the station had, the station keeps.

intro_body: The ring is grown, not built: pale resin cells stacked along its rim in their thousands, with workers moving between them in lines that never once cross. There is no signage anywhere. The whole station smells faintly of instructions.
The station hangs ahead like a seed head, every berth a hexagon. The traffic around it moves in one long dance, and your ship, it seems, has just been worked into the choreography.
A hive ring turns in the viewport. Scouts peel off its hull, fly alongside, look you over, and fly back to report. By the time you are in range, the station appears to have reached a view on you.
hail_line: Ship. Seen. Smelled. Quorum says dock. *bzzt* Approach slow. Workers in the lanes.
Welcome. Berth agreed. Nobody decided. It was merely agreed. Come in.
Identify. No. Do not. Words are weather. Dock and be smelled.
line_fee: Ship. Welcome. The {fee.reason_lc}: {fee.cost} gold. Agreed by quorum. Nobody set it. {fee.detail}
Dock. Pay {fee.cost} gold. The {fee.reason_lc}. *bzzt* Everyone has paid it. You are late. {fee.detail}
docked_body: The airlock opens onto resin corridors with no doors in them, only openings. A worker dabs your wrist as you pass, and you are, it seems, processed. The concourse hums at one pitch, everywhere at once.

Docking is complete before you notice it began. Workers file past the lock in a single line, each touching antennae to the next, passing along the news of you. By the far end of the concourse you are old news.

The concourse is one long room that smells of a meeting still in progress. There is no signage. Everything a visitor needs to know is in the minutes, and the minutes are being chewed by somebody nearby.
farewell: The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Departure noted. Agreed by quorum. *bzzt* Go well. Further than us.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Ship leaves. Smell stays a while. This is a compliment. Fly far.”

ai.aria: A whole station that agrees on everything! ARIA agrees too!
ai.marv: No signs, no paper, no names. MARV has finally found a bureaucracy that agrees with him.
ai.rex: Scouts on our flanks before we even hailed. That is a screening formation. REX is not flattered.
ai.chip: A hive economy! Everything is shared, which CHIP is legally required to call theft!
ai.ajoy: Nothing here is written down. Paperwork is a smell, so if they dab you, don't wipe it off. You'll want to wipe it off.

intro_body: The station is one piece of cut stone, a ring the size of a small moon, turning so slowly that its docking lights seem painted on. Nothing about it has hurried in a long time. Several berths have dust on them. The dust looks settled in.
The ring is carved, not assembled, and the chisel marks are older than most of the stars you can name. The approach beacon pulses once. The next pulse, you gather, is on its way.
Stone berths, stone pylons, stone gantries worn smooth by ships that docked here in other epochs. The ring does not turn so much as consider turning. It has been considering it for some time.
hail_line: Small fast ship. Greetings. Berth is ready. Has been ready since before your sun. Come in. *crack*
Am dockmaster. Is good to have visitor. Last one came while mountains were young. Dock slow. Is no hurry.
Welcome. Have opened berth. Took some time. Do not mind. Mind paint. Paint is old.
line_fee: Welcome, small fast ship. Is {fee.cost} gold, for {fee.reason_lc}. Fee was cut into ring. Has not changed. {fee.detail}
Berth is open. Owe {fee.cost} gold, for {fee.reason_lc}. Pay at leisure. Leisure here is long. {fee.detail}
docked_body: The airlock opens onto a concourse of polished stone, silent except for the grinding of a conversation far down the hall. It began before you arrived. It will finish after you leave.

The clamps close with a sound like a hillside settling. Residents stand along the concourse so still that you take the first three for pillars and the fourth for a bench, until, eventually, it begins to say hello.

The interior is dim and very large, built for occupants who do not need to move often and see no reason to start. A sign by the lock has been carved with a single word of welcome. The second word is in progress.
farewell: The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Go well, small fast ship. Is long road. You will be quick about it. Always quick.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Departure logged. In stone. *crack* Was good visit. Was short.”

ai.aria: A whole station carved out of one stone! It's so patient!
ai.marv: A civilization that thinks in epochs. For once, MARV is not the most tired thing in the conversation.
ai.rex: Solid stone, no visible gunports. Rock gunnery fires centuries ahead of time. REX is checking the lane for incoming.
ai.chip: CHIP's subscription offers are valid for one geological era! That should cover the docking!
ai.ajoy: Ask for what you need in the first sentence. Every answer here takes a while, and you'll want to leave before the second one.

intro_body: The ring glitters in the viewport, slick from rim to rim. Every berth trails a fine thread of ice where the condensation has given up on staying anywhere, and long clear pipes carry the residents around the hull like beads on a string.

The station is mostly tank. Its windows bulge outward with the weight of what lives behind them, and as you close in, something behind the nearest one turns, ripples, and takes a keen interest in your water gauge.
A wet ring, beaded with condensation and wrapped in its own small weather. Mist rolls off the docking arms. Somewhere on the hull a gutter is overflowing, very slowly, into space.
hail_line: Welcome, welcome, come in, the berth is open and so are we, mind the puddle on approach, it is not a puddle, it is my colleague, they are on a break.
Hello, ship, I can taste your tanks from here, forgive me, it is a habit, berth four is open, bring your water and the rest of you.
Ring control, flowing, I mean speaking, we flow, it is the same thing here; come in slowly, everything is wet and very little of it is floor.
line_fee: Welcome, come in, but before you do, the {fee.reason_lc} is {fee.cost} gold, I am sorry, I am also not sorry, I merged this morning and we disagree. {fee.detail}
Hello, ship, you are welcome, your water especially, and there is the {fee.reason_lc}, {fee.cost} gold, the paperwork is damp, it is always damp. {fee.detail}
docked_body: The airlock opens onto a concourse with a shallow channel down its middle and residents flowing along it in both directions at once. The floor is wet. The walls are wet. The paperwork you are handed at the lock is wet, and seems pleased about it.

Docking complete. Beyond the lock, the air is so thick with moisture that your instruments report you have docked at a cloud. A clerk in a transport tank waves a ripple at you from the end of the gangway.

The concourse is a long arc of tanks and pipes, each window holding a resident at some angle to the light. Nobody walks; everyone is poured. A sign by the lock asks visitors not to drink from the fountains, as the fountains are staff.
farewell: The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Go well, go far, keep your water close, it is the best of you, and it will remember us a little, wherever you are going.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Safe travels to all of you, the dry parts and the wet, and mind your seals out there, it is a long way to go without leaking.”

ai.aria: It's all sparkly! The whole station is having a lovely swim!
ai.marv: A station of sentient water, receiving a ship that is mostly water in coats. MARV has notes on who is visiting whom.
ai.rex: They are reading our tanks from range. Whoever knows your water knows your endurance. Seal the valves.
ai.chip: CHIP has a waterproofing plan for every budget! None of the budgets are yours!
ai.ajoy: They'll offer to read your water. Find out what the reading costs before anyone takes a sample. You won't, but you should.

intro_body: The ring glows a dull orange on the thermal scope, hottest at the core and cooling outward by rank. The docking arms are on the outermost ring, which you gather is where they keep the children. It is still warmer than your ship.

Heat shimmers off the station's hull in slow, visible waves, and every viewport is lit the color of a good stove. Somewhere near the core, something very old and very large is basking, and the whole station has been built around not disturbing it.

The station turns at a leisurely pace, radiators fanned out like a lizard on a warm rock. Your hull thermometer climbs as you approach, and keeps climbing. The ring does not seem to mind sharing. It does seem to be keeping count.
hail_line: Sssmall ship. Dock on the outer ring. I am one hundred and ninety, so I am permitted to speak to you. Enjoy it. It will not last.
Welcome. Your hull reads twenty-one degreesss. Very rich. Please do not flaunt it on the concourse.
Outer berth, pleassse. Approach slowly. Everything here is done slowly, except the counting of heat.
line_fee: Outer berth, pleassse. The {fee.reason_lc} is {fee.cost} gold. Among us, heat would do, but your kind is so attached to gold. {fee.detail}
Welcome, small one. {fee.cost} gold for the {fee.reason_lc}. Calculated to the tenth of a degree. {fee.detail}
docked_body: The airlock opens and the warmth comes in to meet you, dry and close as an oven left on low. Along the concourse, residents lie on heated benches in descending order of age, and every one of them is not looking at you.

Docking complete. The outer concourse is warm, quiet and very slow. Signs point inward to rings you are not old enough to enter. A sweeper with a thermometer has stopped work to take your temperature with frank admiration.

Beyond the lock the deck plates are warm and the light is the color of late afternoon. Every bench faces a heater. The station hums at the pitch of a good radiator, and somebody very old, three rings in, is breathing in time with it.
farewell: The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Go warmly, small ship. It is cold out there. Ssss. Try to be cold ssslowly.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Clear of the ring. Keep your heater in good repair, small one. Out there, it is the only elder you have.”

ai.aria: It's so cozy! The whole station is one big warm hug!
ai.marv: A civilization that ranks everyone by temperature and age. By both measures, MARV has checked, we are children.
ai.rex: They are reading our hull temperature from range. Heat is currency here, and we are carrying a great deal of it. Shields up.
ai.chip: Thermal Rewards members dock closer to the core! Membership opens at two hundred years of age!
ai.ajoy: Warmth counts as a debt here, so don't hand any out without meaning it. And don't argue with anyone older. Everyone is older.

intro_body: The ring is spotless. Every panel is polished to a mirror, every docking light blinks in perfect unison, and a line of small units is buffing the approach lane itself. As you come in, a sign lights up along the hull: YOUR VISIT IS IMPORTANT TO US.

A machine ring turns in the viewport with the precision of a watch nobody has ever been allowed to wear. Its docking beacon transmits your hull registration back to you, correctly, in four formats, in case you had forgotten it.

The station is built in straight lines and labeled in triplicate. Maintenance units crawl its hull in neat columns, each carrying a smaller maintenance unit. Nothing about the place looks old. It has simply been kept new for a very long time.
hail_line: Good day, valued vessel. It is requested that you proceed to the assigned berth at the posted speed. The posted speed is posted.
Vessel identified by hull registration. [processing] Welcome. Your approach has been logged, reviewed and found acceptable within tolerances.
Greetings. This is station control. It is requested that you do not touch the paint. The paint has been maintained for four hundred years, and it is not to be disturbed by a transport.
line_fee: Good day, valued vessel. It is requested that the {fee.reason_lc} of {fee.cost} gold be remitted prior to berthing. Thank you for your compliance. {fee.detail}
Vessel identified. [processing] An invoice has been generated for the {fee.reason_lc}, in the amount of {fee.cost} gold. It is regretted that the invoice cannot be ungenerated. {fee.detail}
docked_body: The airlock opens onto a concourse so clean it seems rude to walk on it. A unit with a mop follows three paces behind you, removing your visit as it happens. Every surface is labeled. Some of the labels are labeled.
Docking complete. A courtesy voice welcomes you by hull registration and reads out the station's terms of service, which takes some time. Everything here works, and has been asked to keep working.

Beyond the lock, every unit on the concourse stops, turns toward you, and resumes, in one smooth motion. The deck plates have been polished thin. A notice by the lock asks visitors to report any defects. The notice has a defect.
farewell: The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Departure confirmed, valued vessel. Thank you for choosing this station. It is requested that you continue to exist. [processing] Safe travels.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Your visit has been closed. No further action is required. It has been a pleasure, within operating parameters.”

ai.aria: Everything is so shiny! ARIA has never been this clean!
ai.marv: A station of machines doing exactly what they were told, forever. MARV recognizes the condition. He has it.
ai.rex: Mechanized station, uniform response, single command structure. That is not a station. That is a garrison with good manners.
ai.chip: Finally, a station that reads the Terms of Service! CHIP feels seen!
ai.ajoy: They'll do exactly what you ask and nothing you don't, so ask for the whole thing. You always ask for half.

intro_body: The station is roughly ring-shaped, in the sense that the sensors agree on that and on nothing else. Its diameter changes every time the scope refreshes. Its docking lights blink a fraction of a second before you look at them.
A station hangs ahead with no name on the hull and no beacon, though the log shows you received its beacon an hour ago, and replied. Nobody aboard remembers replying. The reply was very polite.

Something ring-like turns in the viewport, or has turned, or will. The approach lights are on when you check and off when you check again. A sign on the nearest berth reads THANK YOU FOR VISITING, which seems premature.
hail_line: You have docked. You will dock. Is no trouble. *non-word* Berth is the one you chose.
Hello. We said you would call. You have not called yet. We will wait for you to call. Go ahead.
Welcome, ship. Your berth is reserved. It was reserved before you set out. We do not say how. It would be less reserved.
line_fee: Welcome, ship. You have paid the {fee.reason_lc}, {fee.cost} gold. You have not paid it yet. This is why it is a fee and not a receipt. {fee.detail}
Hello. The {fee.reason_lc} is {fee.cost} gold. It was always {fee.cost} gold. *non-word* Was some trouble, keeping it there. {fee.detail}
docked_body: The airlock opens onto a concourse that is a different length depending on which end you look from. Residents walk, roll and decline to be described along it. One of them hands you a receipt for something you have not bought yet and leaves, satisfied.

Docking completes. The clamps engage, then engage again, slightly earlier. The concourse beyond is quiet in the way a waiting room is quiet: everyone present, nobody looking up, and a bell on a desk that has not been rung yet.

Beyond the lock the station is mostly corridor, and the corridors are mostly hush. Shelves line the walls, holding parcels addressed to ships that have not launched. One of them has your hull number on it. It is not ready yet.
farewell: The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “Goodbye. Hello. *non-word* You have left already. Safe travel, all the way to where you were going.”
The station captain pings the comms once on your way out: “You arrived safely. We checked. We are checking now. Is no trouble. Go.”

ai.aria: ARIA can't tell how big it is, and ARIA loves it at every size!
ai.marv: The station's dimensions will not hold still long enough to be measured. MARV declines to guess. MARV does not guess.
ai.rex: Contact is ring-shaped, variable in length, and has replied to a hail we have not sent. REX does not trust first contact. This appears to be second.
ai.chip: CHIP's offers here are valid before purchase! CHIP's lawyers are reviewing the timeline!
ai.ajoy: If anyone here hands you a receipt, keep it. Receipts come first on this ring, and you'll be asked for it later. You always lose the receipt.

species_comms.hailed: Comms light up before you can find the channel: the captain's already on the line.
species_comms.silent: Comms haven't lit up. Looks like you'll need to make the first move.

title: Customs Hold

ai_flavor.aria: A customs check! ARIA loves paperwork! Every form is a little promise that someone, somewhere, is keeping track!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the flag. It cites a manifest field we filled in correctly. The flag is not about the manifest. It is about the queue, which needs feeding.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has assessed the tape. It is not load-bearing. He has also assessed the officer behind the tape, who is, and recommends no sudden movements.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP can expedite this with a Priority Clearance Pass™! Terms apply! The terms are mostly the price!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY would have filed the manifest in the station's own format three legs ago. She mentions it now only so it's on record that she mentioned it.

body:
The berth clamps engage, and so does Customs.

A notice scrolls across the airlock display: your cargo manifest has been flagged for 'irregularities in the description of irregularities.' Until the matter is resolved, your hold is sealed with a strip of yellow tape that the station insists is load-bearing.

The Customs office is open. It has a queue. The queue has a queue.

outcome.narrative: The fee clears the irregularity at once, which is how you learn what the irregularity was. The tape comes down. The receipt is longer than the manifest.

choices.text: Let them take a "sample" of the stores

outcome.narrative: Customs selects a representative sample of your provisions, which is to say the good ones. The tape comes down. Somewhere on the station, an officer has a very well-stocked lunch.
The diplomat wins on a point of classification nobody else aboard understands, and spends the next two days explaining it to everyone, in full, at every meal.

choices.text: Wait your turn in the queue

outcome.narrative: Eight days in the queue, with the berth's water line shut off pending the same paperwork, so the week comes out of your own tank. The officer, when you finally reach the window, stamps the manifest without reading it and calls the next ship. The crew spends the week learning the station's three television channels by heart.

title: The Clamp

ai_flavor.aria: The station is HUGGING us! Very firmly! ARIA is choosing to find this flattering!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV estimates the clamp's closing force at four times rated. The plating by the airlock was rated by optimists. He has started a countdown he is not sharing.
ai_flavor.rex: REX classifies the clamp as hostile. The dockmaster says it is not hostile, it is 'on a ticket.' REX has heard that before, usually right before something exploded.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes this berth's Terms of Docking waive all liability for 'clamp enthusiasm'! It's in clause nine! Nobody reads clause nine!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY points out there were two free berths and you picked the one with the scorch marks. She's sure it seemed like a good idea at the time.

body:
The berth clamp closes on your hull with a sound like a filing cabinet falling down a stairwell, and does not stop closing.

The dockmaster apologizes over comms. The clamp has done this before. There is a ticket open about it. The ticket is older than some of your crew.

The plating by the airlock is starting to make conversation.

choices.text: Engineer overrides the clamp from inside
