outcome.narrative: The engineer opens the clamp's service panel from your side, finds the relay that has been stuck since before the ticket, and hits it with a wrench in a precise and loving way. The clamp lets go. The plating keeps a dent shaped like an apology.
Money changes hands. The clamp, inexplicably, opens at once. The dent it leaves is small, and is described on the receipt as 'normal wear.'

choices.text: Sit tight while the station crew frees you

outcome.narrative: Four days of a maintenance crew arguing about whose clamp it is, while the clamp goes on making its point on your plating and, it turns out, on the water main behind it, which weeps the whole time. It is eventually freed by a junior technician who was not told it couldn't be done.
You burn against the clamp until one of you gives. It is mostly the clamp. The rest is a strip of your plating, now permanently part of the station.

title: Fumigation Notice

ai_flavor.aria: Spa day for the growbay! ARIA is sure the plants will come out refreshed! Mostly refreshed! Some of them will come out!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the fumigant's data sheet. It kills spores. It also kills most things that are not spores, and is mildly hostile to the things it doesn't kill.
ai_flavor.rex: REX respects the officer's commitment. Scorched-earth biosecurity. He would have done the same. He would have done it sooner.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is pleased to offer FumiGuard™ Premium, which kills ninety percent fewer crops than FumiGuard™ Standard! For a modest upgrade fee!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY notes the officer's scanner was calibrated three updates ago. She's not saying the reading is wrong. She's saying it's old, like the officer's opinion of you.

body:
The station's agricultural officer meets you at the airlock with a scanner, a respirator, and the expression of someone who has already decided.

Your growbay has tripped the station's biosecurity threshold. Possibly a spore. Possibly a sensor. The officer does not distinguish between the two, on principle.

The station offers fumigation. The station insists on fumigation. The station has never, in its history, been talked out of fumigation.

outcome.narrative: The growbay is sealed, gassed and vented over two days, and the vent takes some of the ship's air with it. The station is satisfied. The crop is alive, technically, and has the look of something that has been given bad news.

choices.text: Botanist demands a proper culture first

outcome.narrative: The botanist cites three standards and a precedent. The officer runs a real culture, which takes four days and finds a single spore, which the botanist removes by hand, with tweezers and contempt. A few leaves go with it.

choices.text: Pay for the gentle treatment — 15 gold

outcome.narrative: The gentle treatment is the same gas at a lower concentration and a higher price. The crop comes through it singed rather than stunned. The officer signs the release with a pen that cost more than your hull plating.

You decline. The officer logs you as non-compliant, and the station closes every service to a non-compliant ship: no berth, no market, no medbay. You keep the crop exactly as it was, and nothing else from this stop.

intro.title: THE DOCKMASTER'S BOX
intro.body: The dockmaster's office is one desk, one chair and one box. The box is full of letters: paper, in envelopes, addressed in a dozen different hands to the colony you are flying to.
intro.line: Every ship that comes through, I ask. Most say no. Weight allowance, they say. It's eleven grams a letter.

ai.aria: Letters! Real paper ones! ARIA would carry every single one personally if ARIA had hands!
ai.marv: Box mass: two and a half kilograms, box included. Cargo impact: none worth measuring.
ai.rex: Checked the box. Paper. Nothing else.
ai.chip: Courier services are a growth sector! CHIP is just mentioning it!
ai.ajoy: Ask who they're from. Then decide. In that order, ideally.

revisit.body: The box is still on the desk. The dockmaster hasn't moved it.

who.title: THE NAMES
who.body: The dockmaster tips the box toward you so you can read the envelopes. Mothers, mostly. Brothers. A child's handwriting, very large. One addressed simply to 'whoever is in charge out there, please'.
who.line: People who didn't get a berth. Parents of people who did. A few who just want somebody out there to know they're still here.

ai.aria: ARIA is not crying! ARIA has no eyes to cry with! It's very close, though!
ai.marv: Letters in the box: 214. Addressed to named colonists: 187. To 'anyone': 27.
ai.rex: Not my lane. Take the box.
ai.chip: CHIP would like to waive all fees! For once! Don't get used to it!
ai.ajoy: This is the part where you take the box.

letters_take.title: SIGNED FOR
letters_take.body: The dockmaster stamps the box CARRIED BY and writes your ship's name under it, slowly, the way you write a name you mean to remember. The box goes in the hold. It weighs almost nothing. It feels heavier than that.

letters_paid.title: COURIER RATES
letters_paid.body: The dockmaster doesn't argue. They pay in what the station has spare: a crate of station rations, a little dented. You take the box as well. Nobody aboard quite looks at it on the way back to the ship.

letters_decline.title: NEXT SHIP, THEN
letters_decline.body: The dockmaster nods like they expected it, and slides the box back to its place on the desk. 'Next ship, then.' You hear them say it again to the empty office as the door closes.

intro.title: PORT HEALTH
intro.body: A security officer with a clipboard meets you at the office counter, wearing the face of someone who has said 'regrettably' many thousands of times. Your ship has been flagged. The flag reads BIOLOGICAL CARGO, UNDECLARED. It is your crop.
intro.line: Regrettably, live agriculture requires a forty-eight hour inspection. Regrettably, the inspector is on leave. Regrettably, so is the form.

ai.aria: A forty-eight hour inspection! Of our plants! ARIA hopes they pass! ARIA knows they'll pass!
ai.marv: Expedited review fee: 12 gold. Standard wait: 2 days. Inspector availability: unclear.
ai.rex: Officer is armed with a clipboard. The clipboard is winning.
ai.chip: CHIP has a loyalty card for this exact office! It's expired! Regrettably!
ai.ajoy: The crop is the reason. It can be the way out too, if you'd let them see it.

choices.sub: Two days in a holding berth

choices.text: THE MEDIC SIGNS A HEALTH CERTIFICATE
"It's a crop. Come and see it."

revisit.body: The officer is still at the counter. The clipboard hasn't moved.

show.title: THE GROWBAY
show.body: The officer follows you aboard and down to the growbay, clipboard first. Then they see the {crop.name} under the lamps and stop. The clipboard comes down slowly.
show.line: My grandmother grew these. In a window box. I haven't seen a living one in eleven years.

ai.aria: They LOVE it! ARIA knew they would! Everyone loves the crop!
ai.marv: Officer's heart rate: up. Clipboard grip: down. The inspection is over.
ai.rex: Officer stood down.
ai.chip: CHIP recommends a souvenir photo package! It's a beautiful moment! It's billable!
ai.ajoy: Let them stay a minute. I know you're in a hurry. Let them stay.

q_wait.title: CLEARED, EVENTUALLY
q_wait.body: Two days in a holding berth with nothing to do but read the station's safety posters, of which there are forty-one. The inspector returns, glances at the crop for nine seconds and stamps everything. The crew can recite all forty-one posters now.

q_pay.title: EXPEDITED
q_pay.body: The fee clears, the flag clears, and the officer stamps a form that did not exist an hour ago. Expedited review, it turns out, is the same review, faster, and with a receipt.

q_medic.title: CERTIFIED
q_medic.body: {crew.medic} fills in the health certificate at the counter in four minutes flat, in handwriting the officer cannot read and therefore cannot dispute. The flag lifts. The officer looks quietly impressed and asks for the form number, for next time.

q_show.title: INSPECTION COMPLETE
q_show.body: The officer stays twenty minutes and doesn't say much. At the end they sign the inspection form against the growbay wall, mark it PASSED, and leave a station sweet next to the lamp, for the plant. The crew talks about it for days.

intro.title: THE MEMORIAL GARDEN
intro.body: Off the promenade there is a garden no bigger than a cargo bay, and in it, one plant from every colony ship that has ever docked here. Each has a small brass tag with a ship's name. The station botanist is looking at your crop's manifest entry with frank longing.
intro.line: We don't have a {crop.name}. Not one. Would you spare a cutting? A small one. It would get a tag with your ship's name on it.

ai.aria: A garden of every ship! Our crop could be in it! ARIA would like that more than anything! ARIA has said that before! ARIA means it this time!
ai.marv: A cutting costs the crop a little health. It recovers, given time and water.
ai.rex: Garden is secure. Botanist is unarmed. Tags are brass.
ai.chip: A permanent memorial placement is a premium product at most stations! This one is free! CHIP is having complicated feelings!
ai.ajoy: Ask about the garden first. Before anyone starts cutting.

revisit.body: The botanist is back among the brass tags, watering.

garden.title: THE TAGS
garden.body: The botanist walks you along the beds, reading the tags aloud as they go. Some of the plants are thriving. Some are nearly gone. All of them are labeled with the same care.
garden.line: First one came off a ship called the Patience. It never arrived where it was going. The plant did fine, though. They mostly do.

ai.aria: ARIA is reading every tag! ARIA has read all of them twice!
ai.marv: Plants in the garden: 61. Ships recorded as arrived: 44. The other 17 tags are memorials.
ai.rex: Respect.
ai.chip: CHIP has nothing to sell here. CHIP is going to stand quietly for a moment.
ai.ajoy: Now you know what it is. Aren't you glad you asked first?

cut_give.title: A NEW TAG
cut_give.body: The botanist takes the cutting with two fingers and a pair of tiny scissors, as if it might break, and plants it at the end of the row. The new brass tag has your ship's name on it. The crop will miss the leaf for a few days. The crew won't miss the garden at all; they'll remember it.

cut_trade.title: A FAIR TRADE
cut_trade.body: The botanist takes the cutting and hands over a sealed vial of crop treatment from the station's own stores. 'For when it needs it,' they say. 'It will.' The cutting goes into the garden all the same, under a temporary tag.

cut_no.title: MAYBE NEXT TIME
cut_no.body: The botanist nods and goes back to watering. 'Next time, then,' they say, and mean it. The empty space at the end of the row stays empty.

intro.title: A MESSAGE AT THE BAR
intro.body: The robot bartender sets down a coaster in front of you with a name written on it in grease pencil. It's {speaker.name}'s.
intro.line: Somebody's been asking after your {speaker.role}. Sat right there three days running. Says they served together, a long time ago. They're in the corner booth. They look nervous.

ai.aria: An old friend! ARIA loves old friends! ARIA doesn't have any yet! ARIA is working on it!
ai.marv: Corner booth occupant: one human, nervous, on their third cup of something weak.
ai.rex: Checked the booth. Not a threat. Just nervous.
ai.chip: Reunions drive repeat custom! CHIP recommends the bar's two-for-one menu!
ai.ajoy: Let them have this. The schedule will survive one evening, whatever you think.

revisit.body: The coaster is still on the bar. The booth is still occupied.

who.title: THE CORNER BOOTH
who.body: The bartender polishes a glass that is already clean, which is how it thinks.
who.line: Says they owe {speaker.name} their life. Says {speaker.name} would tell it differently. That's usually how you know it's true.

ai.aria: A LIFE DEBT! That's so dramatic! ARIA is invested!
ai.marv: Two versions of one story. The truth is usually in the gap.
ai.rex: Good crew does that. Doesn't talk about it.
ai.chip: CHIP is drafting a feature film! Working title: 'Owed'!
ai.ajoy: Go and say hello. Then let them talk, which means you don't.

friend_evening.title: AN EVENING
friend_evening.body: {speaker.name} spends the evening in the corner booth and comes back at closing, quieter than usual, with red eyes and a station napkin covered in someone's address. They don't say what was talked about. They hum all the way back to the ship.

friend_drinks.title: ON THE SHIP
friend_drinks.body: The whole crew crowds into the corner booth, which was not built for it. The old friend tells the story; {speaker.name} keeps interrupting to say it wasn't like that. It was exactly like that. The bar closes around you. Nobody notices.

friend_brief.title: FIVE MINUTES
friend_brief.body: Five minutes in the booth, a handshake that turns into a hug, and {speaker.name} is back at the ship on time, as ordered. They don't complain. They don't say much of anything until the next station.

title: Fever Ward

ai_flavor.aria: Oh no, they're poorly! ARIA wants to help! ARIA can't catch fevers! ARIA feels that should count for something!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV estimates the fever reaches roughly one in four people who share air for a day. Masks halve that. Staying aboard does better. He notes the station still sells the things you came for.
ai_flavor.rex: REX recommends no contact. He also notes the ship needs what the station has. He has recommended it anyway.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes that the station's loyalty points are DOUBLED during the quarantine! It is the worst promotion CHIP has ever seen! CHIP is still tempted!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says the station needs a medic more than the ship needs the market. If you have one, she'd send them. She suspects you'll go shopping first.

body:
The station is in quarantine, which nobody mentions until the clamps are on.

The dockmaster's hail is tired and very polite: a fever is moving through the ring. Not lethal, mostly. Bad enough. Come aboard if you must, they say. Masks are at the airlock. The medbay is full. The market is open, because it has to be, and so is everything else, at your own risk.

Behind the dockmaster's voice, somebody is coughing.

choices.text: Go aboard with masks, keep it short

outcome.narrative: You mask up and keep every errand short. It isn't short enough. Not long after you leave, one of the crew comes down with the fever: aching, shivering, useless for a week. It will pass. It takes its time.

choices.text: The medic volunteers on the ward

outcome.narrative: {crew.medic} spends eight days on the station's fever ward, working shifts with their own medics until the worst has passed. The station never forgets it: the dockmaster sends a sealed biocomponent culture from the station stores to the airlock on the last day with a note that just says 'thank you'. The crew is proud. The calendar is not.

choices.text: Buy through the airlock and stay sealed

outcome.narrative: You stay sealed and buy what you can through the cargo airlock from a station clerk in a mask: a few crates of food and water, at a handling fee. Nobody aboard sets foot on the ring. Everything else stays out of reach this stop: no market, no medbay, no drydock. Nobody gets sick.

choices.text: Stay sealed and ask to leave
choices.detail: Quarantine holds every departing ship for four days, and closes the market, medbay and drydock to you this stop.

outcome.narrative: You keep the hatch sealed and ask for clearance to leave. Quarantine holds every departing ship four days for observation, so you spend them clamped to a station you never set foot on, and none of its services open to you. The crew understands. The crew is also very, very tired of the ship.

title: Repossession

ai_flavor.aria: They seem very nice! For people taking our fabricator! ARIA is sure there's been a mix-up! ARIA is less sure every second!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has checked the paperwork. It is genuine. It is also forty-one years out of date and assigned twice. He suspects they know that. He suspects they hope you don't.
ai_flavor.rex: REX notes there are two of them and they are not armed. He also notes the station security behind them is. He is keeping his hands visible.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP knows this company! CHIP used to work with them! It was not a good time! Pay them or talk fast! Do not, under any circumstances, sign anything!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says paperwork this old has a hole in it somewhere. Somebody aboard should find it before you sign anything, which she knows is your instinct.

body:
Two people in clean suits are waiting at the airlock when you dock, with a tablet and a document they would like you to read.

The document says your ship's fabricator was leased, not sold, by a company that has since been bought by another company, which has since been bought by the company they work for. The lease was never paid off. They are here to repossess it, or, if you prefer, its most valuable parts.

They are very sorry. They have done this a lot.

outcome.narrative: You pay. The clean suits thank you, stamp the document PAID IN FULL and hand you a receipt that is nearly a meter long. The fabricator stays yours, legally, at last. The gold is gone, which is how this always works.

You let them take the parts. They are quick, careful and thorough: the precision heads, the good feed motors, the calibration crystal. The fabricator still works, more or less, the way a piano still works with some of its keys missing. It will need help.

choices.text: The diplomat finds the hole in the paperwork

outcome.narrative: {crew.diplomat} spends four days in a station office going through forty-one years of contracts line by line. On the fourth afternoon they find it: the lease was assigned twice, and only one of the two companies ever existed. The clean suits read it, look at each other, and leave without saying goodbye. The crew throws the diplomat a dinner.

choices.text: The engineer swaps in a dead unit

outcome.narrative: {crew.engineer} pulls the fabricator's serial plate and bolts it onto a dead unit from the scrap bin while the clean suits are filling in forms. They take the dead unit away very carefully. The real fabricator is a little scraped from the swap. Nobody is proud of it. Nobody gives it back.

title: Strike Day

ai_flavor.aria: A STRIKE! For BETTER CONDITIONS! ARIA supports them completely! ARIA would like to join! ARIA doesn't have conditions!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has read the demands. Rest breaks, safety gear, and a working clamp on berth seven. He rates all three as overdue. He rates the management statement as mostly adjectives.
ai_flavor.rex: REX notes the picket is friendly and the thermos is coffee. He has assessed both as non-hostile. He would like some coffee.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP would like to stress that CHIP is neutral in all labor disputes! CHIP has also donated to the strike fund! CHIP contains multitudes!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says you won't get through the ring without them. Either wait, help, or go round. Shouting at the picket isn't on the list.

body:
The dock workers are on strike.

Nothing is moving. The cargo cranes are parked. The docking clamps are on manual and nobody is touching the manuals. A picket line of dock crew in hi-vis jackets is standing, quite cheerfully, across the entrance to the ring, with a banner and a thermos and a list of demands that is short and entirely reasonable.

The station's management has sent a statement. The statement is longer than the list of demands and does not answer any of them.

outcome.narrative: Four days in a holding berth while management and the picket argue it out. On the fourth day the station agrees to the rest breaks and the safety gear and promises to look at berth seven. The cranes start up again. Everyone cheers. You dock, finally, four days behind.

choices.text: Bring the picket coffee and wait with them

outcome.narrative: You spend four days on the picket line with the dock crew, bringing coffee and sharing {cost.food} points of rations and learning a great deal about berth seven. When the strike ends, they dock you first, by hand, gently, and won't take a tip. The crew comes back aboard with hi-vis jackets nobody can bring themselves to take off.

choices.text: The pilot docks by hand without the clamps

outcome.narrative: {crew.pilot} brings the ship in without the clamps, by hand, against a docking ring that wasn't built for it. It works, mostly. The hull scrapes the collar on the way in with a sound nobody will forget. The picket watches the whole thing and doesn't say a word. They don't have to.

choices.text: Pay into the strike fund to end it sooner

outcome.narrative: You pay into the strike fund, which turns out to be the deciding contribution: the picket can now hold out longer than management can, and management knows it. The strike ends in two days instead of a week. The dock crew docks you first. The gold went somewhere good.

title: The Ring Is Coming Apart

ai_flavor.aria: The station is WOBBLING! ARIA would like it to stop wobbling! ARIA would like to help! ARIA is going to help by being very quiet!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV reads the ring's wobble as growing. The docking arm will hold for perhaps thirty more lurches. He has counted eleven. He has stopped counting out loud.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has every loose object in the ship strapped down. He has also strapped himself down. He recommends everyone else does the same.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP has filed an emergency complaint with the station's management! CHIP has been put on hold! The hold music is very calm! CHIP is not!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says hold the ship to the arm until they stop the spin. Brace for every lurch, together, on the count, which means actually listening to the count. Send a medic if you have one: they're going to need everyone.

body:
You have just docked when the station's spin ring loses a bearing.

The whole ring shudders. Then it starts to wobble, a slow, heavy lurch that sends loose crates sliding along every corridor and sets off every alarm on the station at once. The docking arm holding your ship is on the ring. Every lurch tries to throw the ship off it, and the arm was not built for this.

On the station's emergency channel, the dockmaster is calling for every ship to hold on, and for every medic on the ring to report to the infirmary.

choices.text: Brace the ship to the arm on every lurch

briefing.aria: The ring is lurching and we're on the end of the docking arm! Brace on every lurch and keep us attached!
briefing.marv: The arm holds for perhaps thirty more lurches. Brace against each, ease off between, and we may not need the thirty-first.
briefing.rex: Ring unstable, arm under load. Brace on every lurch. Do not let the arm take the full hit.
briefing.chip: CHIP is still on hold with station management! Meanwhile, brace for every lurch and keep us on that arm!
briefing.ajoy: Brace on the lurch, ease off between. On the count, which means actually listening to it. I'll be counting.

perfect.aria: We rode every lurch! The ring stopped, and the dockmaster came down to shake your hand! In person!
perfect.marv: Every lurch met. The ring is braked, the arm survived, and the dockmaster shook your hand. All three were unlikely.
perfect.rex: All lurches countered. Ship held position until the ring stopped. Dockmaster's thanks noted.
perfect.chip: Every lurch braced! The dockmaster's personal handshake has been added to your loyalty profile!
perfect.ajoy: Every lurch, on the count too. See what listening does. Well done, I suppose.

good.aria: We held on! Two lurches got through and a panel buckled, but the ring stopped and we're still docked!
good.marv: Two lurches unmet, one buckled panel. The arm held. I had given it worse odds than that.
good.rex: Two impacts against the arm. Panel buckled. Position held. Damage is repairable.
good.chip: Docking maintained! The buckled panel is a known lurch-related condition! Not covered, obviously!
good.ajoy: Most of them. The two you missed, the panel shows. I was counting out loud, but sure, it held.

poor.aria: The arm let go and we tumbled, but the thrusters caught us. Someone's hurt, so let's look after them.
poor.marv: The arm let go on the worst lurch and we tumbled a kilometer out. Someone is hurt. The odds were about this.
poor.rex: Lost the arm. Ship tumbled, recovered a kilometer out. One casualty. Get them seen to.
poor.chip: Unscheduled undocking! The thrusters caught us. Someone's hurt, and CHIP is sorry. No upsell. Truly.
poor.ajoy: The arm let go and we tumbled out. Someone's hurt. I did say listen to the count. See to them first.

perfect.narrative: You call every lurch and fire the thrusters against it, and the ship rides the wobbling ring like a boat at anchor in a storm. Two hours later the station brakes the ring to a stop, and the safety checks keep every ship on the arm for two days. Four points of hull. The dockmaster comes down to the berth personally to shake your hand.

good.narrative: Most of the lurches you meet. Two you don't, and the ship slams against the arm hard enough to buckle a panel. The ring stops eventually. Twelve points of hull.

poor.narrative: The arm lets go on the worst lurch and the ship tumbles off the ring and into open space, end over end, with everybody inside it. The thrusters catch it a kilometer out. Twenty points of hull, and someone hurt in the tumble.

outcome.narrative: Everyone braced, the thrusters on standby, and you ride the lurches.

choices.text: Cast off now and get clear

outcome.narrative: You cut the docking arm and fire the thrusters before the next lurch, and the ship tears off the ring with the arm's grapples still in its hull. You get clear. The station stops its ring an hour later, without you. Ten points of hull, and no market, medbay or drydock this stop.

choices.text: Send the medic to the infirmary

outcome.narrative: {crew.medic} goes onto the ring while the rest of the crew holds the ship to the arm. They spend four days in the station infirmary, with the station's medics, through the worst of it. The ship takes some lurches in the meantime. The station takes far fewer casualties than it might have. The dockmaster waives every fee you will ever owe them.

choices.text: Engineer helps them stop the ring

outcome.narrative: {crew.engineer} goes over to the station's bearing room and works with their crew to brake the ring, using your ship's thrusters, on the arm, as an extra brake. It takes two days and a lot of fuel. It works. Six points of hull, six of fuel, and a station engineering team who will name a bearing after you.

title: The Lark

ai_flavor.aria: It's the LARK! ARIA knows them! ARIA has never met them! ARIA feels like she knows them!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV confirms the registry: the Lark, eleven weeks ahead of you once, now stuck. Their drive coupling is a common part. You may have one. Whether you have the hands to fit it is another matter.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has assessed the Lark's crew. Tired. Friendly. Out of noodles. No threat.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the Lark's crew are not customers! They are friends! CHIP is unfamiliar with this category! CHIP is learning!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says they left you half. She'd leave them something back. She's sure you remember. She's mentioning it anyway.

body:
There is a small colony hauler in the next berth, with LARK stenciled on its nose.

It's the same Lark. The crew who left the note on the derelict, the ones who took half and left half. Their ship is in a bad way: a drive coupling gone, a week in dock already, a crew sitting on crates outside their own airlock eating station noodles. When they hear your ship's name, nothing happens. When you tell them about their note, and the one you left next to it, they all stand up at once.

choices.text: Share a crate of supplies with them

outcome.narrative: You haul a crate of your own supplies across the dock, {cost.food} points of food that you can just about spare. The Lark's crew insists on cooking it for everyone, both crews together, on crates, in the berth. It is the best meal of the trip. They promise to leave a note for whoever's next. You believe them.

{crew.engineer} spends two days in the Lark's drive room and gets the coupling running with a part from your own spares. The Lark's crew pays you back the only way they can: five points of fuel from their tank, poured into yours by hand, and a promise to wait for you at the colony with something to drink.

choices.text: Swap route notes over a drink

outcome.narrative: You buy the Lark's crew a round at the station bar and swap notes on the route ahead. Their pilot knows a quieter line past the next hazard. It saves fuel. The drink was worth it before that, though.

choices.text: Wave across the dock and get on with your stop

outcome.narrative: You wave. They wave back. Everybody has a schedule. As your ship undocks, somebody on the Lark's crew holds up a ration wrapper with 'FAIR'S FAIR' written on it in marker, and you laugh all the way out of the berth.

title: The Collector

ai_flavor.aria: A COLLECTOR! Of our BONE! ARIA didn't know the bone was famous! ARIA is so proud of the bone!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV notes the collector's offer will beat any trader's by a distance. He also notes she seems to know what the bone is. That information may be worth more than the money.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has checked the collector. Unarmed. Two pairs of gloves. Very focused. He is not sure which of those worries him most.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP can confirm the collector's coat costs more than the ship! CHIP recommends opening the bidding high! CHIP recommends opening it higher than that!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says ask her what it is before you sell it. You'll want to know what you had, and she'd rather not be the one telling you later.

body:
A woman in a very good coat has been waiting at your berth since before you docked.

She collects fossils, she says. Specifically fossils from low gravity, which she would like to make clear are not really fossils at all, and she has heard (station gossip travels faster than ships) that you are carrying one. She would very much like to see it. She has brought gloves. She has brought a second pair of gloves in case the first pair is not enough.

outcome.narrative: She turns it over in her gloved hands for a long time without speaking, then pays thirty gold without haggling, which tells you it was worth a great deal more. She wraps it in three layers of cloth and walks away holding it like a baby.

choices.text: Trade it for her old star chart

outcome.narrative: She doesn't have the gold on her, she says, but she has something better: a fragment of nav data from a survey she ran years ago, still accurate. Use it, she says, and you'll know what's at the next stop before you get there. You shake on it. She is very careful not to let go of the bone first.

choices.text: Ask her what it is, and keep it

outcome.narrative: She tells you, at length, over a cup of station tea.

log_lore.title: NOT A BONE
log_lore.text:
The collector's account, as recorded:

'It's a cast. Something grew here, very slowly, in very low gravity, on the inside of a hollow rock. It grew for a long time — longer than people have existed. Then it died, and minerals filled the space where it had been, one molecule at a time, and kept its shape.

'Nobody knows what it was. That's why I want it. That's why you should keep it.'

She did not offer a second time.

title: Return to Sender

ai_flavor.aria: It's his GRANDMOTHER'S! After sixty YEARS! ARIA is going to cry! ARIA can't cry! ARIA is doing the face!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has checked the details he gave against the object. All of them match. The odds of this are very poor. He would like to stop working out the odds, just this once.
ai_flavor.rex: REX confirms no threat. REX confirms one very old man, holding very still.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP's appraisal database values the artifact at forty gold! CHIP would like to say that is the wrong number! CHIP does not have the right number!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says you already know what you're going to do. She'd have done it faster. Do it.

body:
An old man at the station market stops dead when he sees your hold manifest on the trader's screen.

The pre-collapse artifact. He describes it before you show it to him: the chip in the corner, the maker's mark, the small repaired crack along the base. It was his grandmother's. She sent it ahead on a colony ship sixty years ago, when the evacuations started, so that something of hers would arrive somewhere. The ship never did.

You are holding the only thing that did.

outcome.narrative: You put it in his hands. He doesn't say anything for a long while. Then he tells you about his grandmother: her garden, her terrible singing, the way she packed this into a crate with her own hands and said 'something should get there.' Something did. The crew walks back to the ship without talking much, and every one of them is glad.

He insists on paying, and won't take it any other way, and you settle on a fair price that is less than a fence would give and more than you'd have asked anyone else. He holds it all the way out of the market.

You keep it. He nods as if he expected nothing else, thanks you for letting him see it, and walks away slowly through the market. The artifact sits in the hold afterwards, and nobody likes walking past it.

title: The Last Employee

ai_flavor.aria: He WORKED there! For thirty-one YEARS! ARIA would like to give him everything! ARIA has nothing to give! ARIA would give him a hug! ARIA has no arms!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV estimates the maintenance chief's drydock work at well above the memorabilia's sale value. He also estimates the chief would take it for nothing. He would rather not test that.
ai_flavor.rex: REX notes the chief still salutes the logo. REX respects loyalty to a unit, even a dissolved one.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP is very moved! CHIP also knew this company! CHIP worked with them briefly! It ended badly! For the company!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says trade it for the repair. He'll want to give you something for it. Let him, and don't haggle, for once.

body:
The station's maintenance chief spots the logo on the memorabilia in your hold and goes very quiet.

He worked for them, he says. Thirty-one years, man and boy, right up until the morning they locked the doors and nobody came back to unlock them. He still has his badge. He still does his rounds the way they taught him. He has never once seen the logo since, outside his own locker.

He'd like it, he says, if you'd part with it. He doesn't have much. He has a drydock and a very long memory for favors.

choices.text: Trade it for a hull repair

outcome.narrative: He takes the memorabilia in both hands, polishes the logo with his sleeve, and puts it on the shelf above his workbench. Then he and his crew patch your hull for free, and won't hear a word about payment, and do it to a standard the company itself would have been proud of. The welds are better than new.
He pays twelve gold for it, counting it out of an old company wage envelope he's kept for exactly this kind of occasion. He shakes your hand like it's a contract.

choices.text: Keep it and hear his stories

outcome.narrative: You keep it, but you buy him a drink, and he tells you what the company was like: the parties, the scandals, the fire drill that became an actual fire. The crew laughs until the bar closes. He leaves happy. The memorabilia stays in the hold, slightly more famous than before.

title: The Other Botanist

ai_flavor.aria: ANOTHER botanist! With the SAME crop! ARIA wants them to be friends! ARIA can sense they are not going to be friends!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has reviewed the other ship's public growbay figures. Their crop is about level with yours. They do not seem to know that. He will not be telling them.
ai_flavor.rex: REX notes the other botanist has a soil probe. He has assessed the soil probe as a weapon. He has concluded it is not one. He is keeping an eye on it.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP sees a sponsorship opportunity! A crop-off! Two colony ships! One winner! CHIP would sell tickets!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says you can make a friend or a rival here. Both will remember you at the next station. She'd pick friend. She suspects you'll pick whichever wins the comparison.

body:
There is another colony ship in the next berth, and its botanist has come over to look at your crop.

They are carrying a crop of their own: a {crop.name}, as it happens, in a bay the same size, bound for a colony of their own. They would very much like to compare. They have brought notes. They have brought a soil probe. They have brought, it becomes clear quite quickly, the strong opinion that their crop is doing better than yours.

outcome.narrative: You walk them through your growbay and they walk you through theirs, and somewhere between the soil probes and the watering schedules it stops being a competition. You trade contact codes at the airlock. They promise to leave something for you at the next station.

You tell them, politely, that your crop is doing better than theirs. They tell you, less politely, that it isn't. The crew enjoys the whole thing enormously. The other botanist leaves with a look that suggests this is not over.

Two days of trading techniques over station tea: their trick for root rot, your trick for leaf curl, an argument about water timing that both of you win. Your crop comes out of it better. So, presumably, does theirs.

title: A Parcel at the Dock

ai_flavor.aria: A PRESENT! From our botanist FRIEND! ARIA is so happy! ARIA has never been given a present! ARIA has technically still not been given one, but it feels like it!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV identifies the parcel's contents by weight and shape as a vial of crop treatment. A practical gift. The best kind.
ai_flavor.rex: REX has scanned the parcel. Safe. He has also scanned the note. Friendly. He is pleased.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP notes the parcel came with free shipping! Between friends! CHIP has never seen this business model! CHIP is moved!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says open it, and send something back. She'll draft the thank-you note, since someone has to.

body:
There's a parcel waiting at the dockmaster's desk with your ship's name on it.

It's from the other botanist, the one with the same crop, who docked here two days ahead of you and has gone on. The parcel is small and carefully wrapped, and the note taped to it is in a botanist's tiny, precise handwriting: 'Found this at the market. Thought of your back row. Good luck out there. Don't let mine beat you.'

outcome.narrative: Inside: a vial of crop treatment, and a pressed leaf from their crop, labeled 'for luck'. The treatment goes into the hold for when the crop needs it. The leaf goes up on the growbay wall.

choices.text: Open it and leave something in return

outcome.narrative: You take the vial of treatment and leave a parcel of your own at the dockmaster's desk for their next stop: some of the good rations, {cost.food} points of them, and a note in your own handwriting. The crew argues for an hour about what the note should say, which is the best hour anyone's had this week.

title: Footprints in the Growbay

ai_flavor.aria: Someone SNUCK in! To see our CROP! ARIA is outraged! ARIA is also a little flattered!
ai_flavor.marv: MARV has the growbay logs. Someone was in the bay for nine minutes. Nothing was taken. Something was measured. He would like to know what.
ai_flavor.rex: REX recommends confronting the suspect immediately. He has identified the suspect. He has prepared a stern expression.
ai_flavor.chip: CHIP must point out that corporate espionage is a serious matter! CHIP has done some! CHIP knows how serious it is!
ai_flavor.ajoy: AJOY says check the crop before you march over there. You'll want to know what they did before you ask them why.

body:
Someone has been in your growbay while you were docked.

There are footprints in the spilled soil by the back row, boots, not crew issue. One of the pots has been moved an inch to the left. The soil probe readings jumped at about the time the other colony ship docked in the berth next to yours, and the botanist on that ship, the one who was so sure their crop was better than yours, is the only person on the station who would care.

outcome.narrative: You march over to the other ship and demand an explanation. The other botanist, red-faced, admits it: they only wanted to measure your soil, because yours was doing better and they couldn't work out why. It is very hard to stay angry at someone who has just told you that your crop is better. You manage it for about a minute.

You check the crop. Nothing's damaged. In fact the pH on the back row has been corrected, a problem you hadn't spotted, and there's a folded note tucked under the moved pot: 'Your soil was too acid. Fixed it. Don't tell anyone I was here.' The crew decides, unanimously, never to tell anyone.

choices.text: Lock the growbay and say nothing

outcome.narrative: You change the growbay's lock code, say nothing, and keep a close eye on the other ship until it leaves. Nothing else happens. You never find out what they were doing in there. That bothers everyone for longer than it should.
